Employees are eligible for a maximum of 7 casual leave days per calendar year. Casual leave is granted on a first‑come, first‑served basis and must be applied through the HR portal at least 48 hours prior to the intended date, except in cases of medical emergencies where a doctor’s certificate may be submitted within 24 hours.  

Eligibility: full‑time employees who have completed a minimum of 3 months of continuous service are eligible. New employees (0–3 months) are not eligible for casual leave; they may avail of 2 compensatory off days for personal commitments after completion of their probation.

Employees who are permanently employed on a full‑time basis and have completed a minimum of 6 months of continuous service are eligible to avail casual leave. The entitlement is 5 working days per calendar year. This leave can be taken for personal emergencies, unforeseen events, or short‑term medical appointments. Casual leave cannot be carried over beyond 2 days into the next calendar year; any unused days beyond this limit are forfeited. Employees who are on contractual or part‑time arrangements are not eligible for casual leave unless expressly granted in the contract.

During the first 12 months, employees may take up to 3 casual days per month, subject to supervisory approval and ensuring no disruption of client call volumes. In case of a national holiday falling on a scheduled workday, the holiday is not counted against casual leave. Casual leave cannot be combined with other leave types. Employees in managerial or supervisory roles may be granted up to 2 additional casual days per year for unforeseen operational issues, subject to board approval. The company reserves the right to refuse casual leave if the request would compromise client service levels.

Employees who have completed a minimum of three months of continuous service are eligible for Casual Leave (CL). A full‑time employee is entitled to a maximum of seven (7) CL days per financial year (01 April – 31 March). The CL can be taken in one or more segments, each not exceeding five (5) consecutive days. Employees may carry forward a maximum of five (5) unused CL days to the next financial year; any remaining days will be forfeited. Part‑time and contractual staff are not entitled to CL under this policy. Casual Leave can be availed for personal emergencies, medical appointments, or unforeseen circumstances, but not for routine or planned absences. Requests must be submitted through the online HR portal at least 48 hours prior to the intended start date, except in genuine emergencies where a written explanation will be accepted within 24 hours. In cases of bereavement, the employee may be granted up to three (3) CL days within a 30‑day period. For maternity leave, the employee will be eligible for the statutory 26 weeks of paid leave, which supersedes CL. The bank reserves the right to deny CL if the employee has exceeded the annual limit or if operational exigencies arise.

Employees eligible for casual leave after completing 3 months of continuous service. Each fiscal year employees are entitled to 5 days of casual leave. Casual leave can be taken for personal reasons, medical emergencies, or unavoidable circumstances. Unused casual leave cannot be carried forward and will be forfeited at year‑end. Employees in supervisory or managerial positions may request up to 2 additional days per year, subject to approval, if work can be temporarily delegated. Casual leave cannot be taken as a substitute for sick leave or unpaid leave. Employees on maternity or paternity leave are exempt from casual leave for the duration of the statutory leave. In exceptional cases, such as natural disasters or national emergencies, the Board may authorize up to 3 extra days per employee, with documentation. All casual leave requests must be submitted through the HR portal at least 48 hours in advance, unless in an emergency. The policy applies to full‑time and part‑time staff, excluding interns and volunteers.

Employees are entitled to casual leave (CL) for unforeseen personal or family emergencies. CL is granted at a rate of 2 days per month of continuous service, capped at a maximum of 12 CL days per calendar year. An employee must have completed a minimum of 3 months of continuous service to be eligible for CL. CL days may be taken only with the prior approval of the immediate manager, and must be applied at least 48 hours before the intended leave unless in genuine emergency circumstances. CL cannot be carried forward beyond the next calendar year; unused CL days expire at the end of the year, except for employees in the store management tier who are exempt from this carry‑over rule. Employees who have taken more than 10 CL days in a year will be required to submit a written justification to HR, and further CL requests will be reviewed on a case‑by‑case basis. CL days are paid at the employee’s basic salary rate and do not affect the employee’s gratuity calculation. Accrued CL days beyond the statutory 12 days are forfeited and will not be paid out at termination.

Employees are entitled to a total of five (5) casual leave (CL) days per calendar year.  The leave can be taken in any combination of single days or multiple days, but no more than two (2) consecutive CL days are allowed during a normal production cycle.  Casual leave is payable at 100 % of the basic salary for the first three (3) days, 50 % for the next two (2) days, and is unpaid thereafter.  Unused CL days may be carried forward to the next year up to a maximum of two (2) days; any remaining days beyond this limit are forfeited.  Eligibility: full‑time employees who have completed a minimum of three (3) months of continuous service are eligible to apply for CL.  Employees on probation or those who have not reached the three‑month threshold may request CL, but it will be considered at the discretion of the supervisor and will not be paid.  Exceptions: CL may be granted for medical emergencies, urgent family matters, or unavoidable personal commitments, provided the employee submits a written reason and supporting documentation within 48 hours of the event.  CL requests must be submitted via the HR portal at least three (3) business days in advance, except in cases of emergency.

Employees are eligible for casual leave to accommodate unforeseen personal matters. Each full‑time employee who has completed a minimum of 3 months of continuous service may avail up to 7 casual leave days per calendar year. The leave accrues at a rate of 0.2 days per month of service, but can be carried forward only up to 3 days; any excess is forfeited. Senior managers and above (designated by the HR office) are permitted a maximum of 10 casual leave days per year. Contractual staff and remote workers are eligible for 5 days per year under the same 3‑month service threshold. Casual leave cannot be taken during declared peak project periods or in lieu of sanctioned leave types. Requests must be submitted through the HR portal at least 24 hours in advance and approved by the immediate supervisor; emergency situations may be considered with a supporting medical or police report. Exceptions are granted for bereavement (within immediate family), natural disasters, or any government‑issued emergency. Unapproved absence will be treated as unauthorized leave and may result in disciplinary action.

Casual Leave (CL) is granted to all full‑time employees who have completed a minimum of 3 months of continuous service. Each employee is entitled to 10 CL days per calendar year, subject to the following conditions:

• CL must be taken in whole days; half‑day requests are permitted only with manager approval and must be booked at least 48 hrs in advance.  
• Unused CL days may be carried forward to the next calendar year, but only up to a maximum of 5 days. Any balance beyond 5 days is forfeited.  
• CL can be availed for personal emergencies, short‑term family events, or sudden illness. The employee must notify the immediate manager and HR via the leave portal within 2 hrs of the event.  
• For part‑time or contract staff, CL is pro‑rated on a monthly basis (e.g., 0.83 days per month for a 20‑hour week).  
• CL cannot be converted into cash or used for vacation purposes. Excessive misuse (more than 3 CL days in a single month) will trigger a review by HR and may result in disciplinary action.

Employees eligible for casual leave are those who have completed a minimum of six months of continuous service in a regular contract. Full‑time staff are entitled to 12 days of casual leave per calendar year, while part‑time staff receive 1 day for every 20 days worked, capped at 8 days. Casual leave may be carried forward no more than 5 days to the next year; any balance beyond this is forfeited. Leave may not exceed 10 % of the employee’s total working days in a year. Requests must be submitted via the HR portal at least 48 h in advance, except in cases of sudden illness or emergency. Casual leave can be taken up to 2 consecutive days without prior approval; longer periods require managerial consent. Exceptions include bereavement (up to 3 days), childbirth (up to 5 days for mothers), and documented medical emergencies, for which a medical certificate is required. Probationary staff and interns are exempt from casual leave. Unauthorised absences will be treated as unrecorded leave and may lead to disciplinary

Employees are entitled to casual leave (CL) as per the PSU’s Leave Policy, with a maximum of 10 CL days per calendar year for employees who have completed at least 12 months of continuous service. New hires and employees on probationary period are allowed 5 CL days in the first 12 months, thereafter the full 10 days accrue. Senior Management (Grade A and B) are granted 15 CL days annually. CL may be taken for unforeseen personal or family circumstances such as urgent medical treatment, emergency travel, or bereavement, without prior formal approval, though the employee must report the leave within 24 hours to the immediate supervisor and submit a brief written note within 48 hours. CL cannot be carried over beyond 5 days; any remaining balance at year‑end is forfeited. Accumulation of CL beyond the statutory limit of 10 days (or 15 for senior staff) is prohibited. In exceptional cases where CL is required for extended family emergencies, the employee may request an extension, which is granted only after written justification and managerial approval. The total CL utilisation shall not exceed 5 % of the employee’s sanctioned working days in a fiscal year.

All full‑time employees are entitled to a maximum of 12 paid sick days per calendar year. Employees who have completed a minimum of 30 consecutive days of service are eligible to accrue sick leave; new hires on probationary periods accrue 6 days per year, which convert to 12 days upon successful completion of the probation. Sick leave is paid at 100 % of the employee’s basic salary. Each leave request must be accompanied by a medical certificate from a registered practitioner for absences exceeding 48 hours. The company permits a carry‑over of up to 5 unused sick days to the next calendar year; any balance beyond 5 is forfeited. Employees on extended medical leave (≥30 days) must provide a doctor’s recommendation and may be eligible for an unpaid leave of absence. Mental health days are treated as sick leave; employees may claim up to 3 such days annually without a medical certificate. All sick leave requests are logged in the HRIS and approved by the immediate supervisor within 24 hours. Accumulated unused sick leave beyond the carry‑over limit is not paid out upon termination.

All permanent employees who have completed a continuous service of at least 90 days are eligible for paid sick leave. Employees may avail up to 10 paid sick days in a calendar year. The first 5 days are paid at 100% of the basic salary, days 6‑10 are paid at 80% of basic salary. Any unused sick leave beyond 5 days must be reported to the HR department within 3 days of the start of the leave, and a medical certificate from a registered doctor is required. Sick leave is non‑carryable; the employee must use the days within the same calendar year. Employees who have joined within the last 90 days are entitled to 5 days of paid sick leave, payable at 80% of basic salary. Exceptions apply for employees with chronic or long‑term illnesses, where an employer may allow a maximum of 30 additional days per year, subject to a medical review and approval by the Medical Advisory Board. Employees injured on the job are entitled to paid sick leave as per the Workmen’s Compensation Act, irrespective of the annual limit. All other leaves (e.g., bereavement, maternity) are governed by separate policies.

Sick leave shall be granted to all regular employees on medical grounds. Each employee is entitled to a maximum of 30 days of paid sick leave per calendar year. In cases where a medical certificate is presented, the leave is fully paid at the employee’s basic salary. For leave exceeding 5 days without a medical certificate, the employee must provide a doctor’s note within 48 hours of the leave start date; otherwise, the leave will be treated as unpaid. Employees who have completed at least 12 months of continuous service are eligible for sick leave; those with less than 12 months are not. Employees on a contractual basis may avail up to 15 days of sick leave per year. Sick leave can be carried forward up to a maximum of 5 days into the next calendar year; any unused leave beyond that limit will be forfeited. Exceptions: Employees with a certified chronic illness or disability, as recognized by a medical board, may be granted additional leave up to 15 days per year. In case of a national lockdown or pandemic, the company may extend the paid sick leave limit up to 45 days.

Employees are entitled to 12 paid sick days per fiscal year, with an additional 3 days that can be taken at 80% pay if a medical certificate is provided. A maximum of 15 days can be availed in any 12-month period. Employees must be employed for at least 3 months to qualify. All sick leaves beyond 2 consecutive days require a medical certificate issued by a registered doctor. Leaves taken for minor illnesses that do not exceed 2 days are exempt from certification. Sick leave can be carried forward up to 5 days into the next fiscal year. No sick leave is granted for absences due to personal reasons or non-medical causes. In case of pregnancy, an employee is entitled to 12 days of maternity leave as per the Maternity Benefit Act, plus an additional 7 days of paid sick leave within the same period. Employees must report their absence within 2 hours of shift start and submit a medical certificate within 24 hours of return. Failure to comply may result in leave adjustment or disciplinary action.

All permanent and contract employees who have completed a continuous service period of at least 30 days are eligible for paid sick leave.  Each employee accrues 2 sick‑leave days per month, with a maximum accrual of 24 days per calendar year.  The company allows a carry‑over of up to 5 days into the next fiscal year; any unused days beyond this limit will be forfeited.  For the first 10 consecutive days of illness, the employee receives 100 % of the basic salary.  From day 11 to day 20, pay is reduced to 50 % of the basic salary.  Sick leave beyond 20 days requires a medical certificate and may be subject to audit.  In case of a chronic or long‑term illness, a doctor’s note can extend the permissible leave to a maximum of 30 days per year, provided it is approved in writing by the HR Manager.

Exceptions:  
• Maternity leave (26 weeks), paternity leave (5 days), bereavement leave (3 days) and COVID‑19 isolation (up to 10 days) are treated separately and do not count against the annual sick‑leave quota.  
• Unpaid sick leave is permitted only after exhaustion of the 24‑day annual allotment.  

All sick‑leave requests must be submitted through the HR portal, with a medical certificate attached for any absence exceeding 2 consecutive days.

All employees who have completed a continuous service of at least 3 months are eligible for paid sick leave. Each employee is entitled to 15 paid sick leave days per calendar year. Out of these, 5 days can be taken without a medical certificate; the remaining 10 days require a valid medical certificate from a registered hospital or doctor. No more than 2 paid sick leave days may be taken in a single calendar month. The first 10 paid sick leave days will be compensated at 100 % of the employee’s basic salary; any sick leave taken beyond the first 10 days will be paid at 70 % of the basic salary. Employees may carry forward up to 5 unused sick leave days to the next calendar year; any balance beyond 5 days will be forfeited. Eligible employees are required to submit a medical certificate from a registered doctor for any sick leave exceeding two consecutive days. Full‑time staff who have completed their probationary period of 90 days are entitled to 12 paid sick days per calendar year. The first seven days of sick leave are paid at 100 % of the employee’s basic salary; days eight to twelve are paid at 50 % of basic salary. Any unused sick days may be carried forward up to a maximum of 5 days to the following year, after which they lapse. Employees on part‑time or contractual engagement are entitled to pro‑rated sick days based on the number of hours worked, with a maximum of 6 days per year. Sick leave may be taken for the employee’s own illness or for a child under 12 years suffering from a contagious disease, in which case a single day of leave is granted per illness episode, subject to a medical certificate. The organization reserves the right to request a second opinion from a corporate medical panel for repeated absences. All sick leave must be recorded in the HR portal within 48 hours of return.

Employees who have completed a minimum of 3 continuous months of service are eligible for Privilege (Earned) Leave. The entitlement is calculated annually and accrues on a monthly basis at a rate of 1/12 of the annual entitlement. The leave schedule is as follows: 10 days for the first year of service, 15 days for the second and third years, 20 days for the fourth and fifth years, and 25 days thereafter up to a maximum of 30 days per annum. Only full‑time permanent staff are eligible; contractual, part‑time, and volunteer staff are not covered under this policy.

Leave may be carried over to the next calendar year up to a maximum of 5 unused days. Any remaining balance beyond this limit will be forfeited. Employees may encash up to 5 days of accrued leave per year, subject to approval by the HR Manager and after ensuring no critical operational impact. Leave must be taken in whole‑day increments, except for medical emergencies where half‑day leave is permitted. Unapproved absences will be deducted from the employee’s leave balance. This policy supersedes any earlier leave arrangements and is effective from 1 January 2026.

Employees are eligible for Privilege (Earned) Leave after completing a continuous minimum of 12 months of service. Accrual is calculated on a pro‑rated basis at 1.25 days per month, equivalent to 15 days per calendar year. Accrued leave may be taken after the 12th month and can be applied for in 5‑day increments. The maximum leave that can be accrued and carried forward into the next calendar year is capped at 5 days. Unused leave beyond this limit will be forfeited at year‑end. Leave can be utilized for personal, family, or health reasons, subject to prior approval from the employee’s immediate supervisor and HR. Exceptions to accrual rules include: (i) Medical emergency leave as per the company’s Medical Leave Policy; (ii) Maternity leave of 12 weeks and paternity leave of 5 days; (iii) Bereavement leave of up to 3 days; and (iv) Unpaid leave in cases of disciplinary action or resignation. Employees on contractual or probationary status are not eligible for earned leave until the completion of the probation period.

All full‑time employees are entitled to 15 days of paid Privilege (Earned) Leave per financial year (01‑04 to 31‑03). Leave is accrued at 1.25 days per month, starting from the first day of employment, and can be taken in full‑day increments only. Accrued leave is credited once a calendar month is completed; any leave accrued in the month of resignation or termination is payable as per the standard settlement policy.

Eligibility: Employees must have completed a minimum of 6 consecutive months of service and be on a regular employment contract (not probationary). Employees on temporary contracts, interns, or part‑time arrangements are ineligible unless explicitly approved in writing by HR. Employees who have not met the minimum service requirement may request leave under a “Leave Without Pay” scheme, which is subject to managerial approval.

Carry‑forward: At year end, employees may carry forward a maximum of 5 unused days to the next financial year. Any balance beyond 5 days is forfeited. Employees must submit a leave request at least 7 days in advance; emergency leave will be considered on a case‑by‑case basis. Exemptions: New hires joining after 01‑04 are eligible for prorated leave from the day of joining, and leave taken for a medical emergency is treated as medical leave, not counted against earned leave.

Employees who have completed at least 6 months of continuous service are eligible for Privilege/Earned Leave (PEL). Leave accrues at 1.5 days per month (18 days per year). Employees with more than 5 years of uninterrupted service accrue at 2 days per month (24 days per year). The maximum PEL that can be carried forward to the next calendar year is 10 days; any balance beyond this is forfeited unless approved by HR for special circumstances. PEL must be taken in a minimum block of 2 days and cannot be split into single‑day increments. Requests must be submitted at least 7 days in advance and approved by the immediate supervisor. PEL can be used for personal reasons, family care, or health issues; for medical emergencies, a doctor’s certificate is required within 48 hours. PEL is not transferable to cash or other benefits. In the event of termination, accrued but unused PEL is paid out at the employee’s current basic salary rate. Employees on a contractual or part‑time basis are not eligible for PEL under this policy.

Privilege/earned leave is accrued at a rate of 0.5 day per month of continuous service, capped at 30 days. Employees with at least 3 months of continuous service are eligible. Leave accrual is pro‑rated for employees who join after the start of a calendar year. For each completed year, an additional 5 days is granted, up to a maximum of 30 days. Accrued leave may be carried forward for up to 90 days beyond the end of the financial year; any balance exceeding 90 days will be forfeited. Employees on permanent assignment are eligible; contractual and temporary staff are excluded. Maternity leave of 12 weeks is granted separately and does not count against privilege leave. Employees with less than 3 months of service are ineligible. For employees who resign or are terminated before completing 12 months, 20% of the accrued leave is forfeited. Leave may be taken in a minimum of 2‑day blocks. Approval is required from the immediate supervisor and HR. Unused leave beyond the carry‑forward limit will be paid out at the employee’s current basic pay.

Employees who have completed at least two (2) consecutive years of service are eligible for Privilege (Earned) Leave under this policy. The leave entitlement is 12 days per calendar year, calculated on a pro‑rated basis for employees who join after 1 January. Each leave day is valued at 5 % of the employee’s basic salary for the purpose of leave encashment, but encashment is permitted only if the employee has exhausted the full 12 days and has not taken leave in the last six (6) months. Leave can be taken in blocks of at least one day and must be scheduled at least fourteen (14) days in advance, except in cases of emergency.

Maximum carry‑forward: a maximum of five (5) unused leave days may be carried forward to the next calendar year; any balance beyond this is forfeited. Employees on permanent disability or with a medical certificate of at least thirty (30) days may apply for an extension up to an additional ten (10) days, subject to approval by the HR Manager.

Exceptions: new hires are not entitled to privilege leave until the completion of the two‑year period; maternity leave (as per the Maternity Benefit Act) and bereavement leave are separate and not counted against the 12-day entitlement. This policy supersedes any earlier leave provisions and is governed by the bank’s internal regulations and applicable Indian labor laws.

Full‑time employees who have completed a minimum of 12 months of continuous service are entitled to 15 days of paid privilege leave per financial year (April‑March). For every additional 30 days worked beyond the first year, employees earn an extra 1 day of leave, capped at 30 days in a year. Employees on a probationary period of up to 3 months are exempt from accruing leave. Part‑time and contract staff accrue leave on a pro‑rated basis (0.5 day per 30 days of work). Leave can be taken in increments of a minimum of 2 days. Unused leave may be carried forward to the next year up to a maximum of 10 days; any balance beyond that is forfeited. Employees may encash up to 5 days of accrued leave at 10% of the basic salary per day, subject to board approval. Exceptions apply: maternity leave of 12 weeks, paternity leave of 2 days, bereavement leave of 3 days, and medical leave beyond 3

Employees are eligible for privilege/earned leave after completing 90 consecutive days of service. Full‑time staff accrue 12 days per calendar year, plus 2 additional days for each full year of service beyond the first year, capped at 30 days. Leave accrues monthly at 1 day per month. A maximum of 10 days may be carried forward into the next fiscal year; any balance beyond this will be forfeited at year‑end. Employees on maternity, paternity, or medical leave do not accrue privilege leave during the leave period, but may carry over unused balance up to the 10‑day limit. Contractual employees and interns are not eligible for privilege leave. Leave must be applied for through the HR portal at least 7 days in advance and approved by the immediate manager; emergency requests may be granted at the discretion of the manager. Upon resignation, any unused privilege leave will be paid out at the current basic salary rate, subject to the 10‑day carry‑over limit. For any clarification, contact the HR Helpdesk (hrhelp@company.com).

Employees who have completed a continuous period of 12 months are eligible for privilege leave of 30 paid days per calendar year. In addition, earned leave is accrued at a rate of 1.5 days per month (totaling 18 days per year) and may be applied for any purpose. The maximum number of earned leave days that can be carried forward into the next year is 10 days; any surplus will be forfeited. New employees are eligible for earned leave after 3 months of continuous service, whereas privilege leave eligibility is deferred until the completion of the first full year. Senior medical and administrative staff with a tenure of more than 5 years may request an additional 5 days of earned leave per annum, subject to board approval. Leaves exceeding 30 days in a calendar year are considered unpaid and must be reported to HR. Unused privilege leave may be taken as unpaid leave or converted into cash settlement only after 5 years of service, in compliance with the Hospital Staff Act. For exceptional circumstances (e.g., death of a family member, serious illness), up to 7 additional days may be granted without penalty.

Employees who complete a minimum of one (1) year of continuous service with the Company are eligible to accrue Privilege/Earned Leave (PEL). The accrual schedule is as follows: 12 days per calendar year for employees with 1 to 5 years of service, 15 days per year for 5 to 10 years, and 18 days per year for those with more than 10 years of service. Accrued leave may not exceed 30 days in any calendar year; any balance beyond this cap will be forfeited unless the employee obtains written approval from the HR Manager for a special leave extension, which is granted only in exceptional circumstances (e.g., chronic illness, severe family emergencies). Leave must be taken in a minimum of one (1) day blocks unless otherwise approved by the immediate supervisor. PEL can be carried over for a maximum of 60 days to the following year; any unused leave beyond this limit will be terminated. For employees engaged in overtime or night shifts, an additional 2 days of PEL per year is granted as a compensatory benefit. In case of medical emergencies, the employee may avail up to three (3) days of emergency leave without using PEL. All PEL requests must be submitted at least seven (7) days in advance and approved through the standard leave application portal.

Employees who have completed a continuous service of at least 12 months before the date of expected delivery are eligible for maternity leave. The bank provides a total of 26 weeks of paid maternity leave, which can be taken in two consecutive periods: a minimum of 4 weeks at the end of the pregnancy and the remainder after delivery. For the first 12 weeks of leave, employees receive 100% of their basic salary; for the subsequent 14 weeks, the bank pays 30% of basic salary, in accordance with the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017. Employees who are on probation or have not completed the 12‑month tenure are not eligible for paid leave; however, they may avail of unpaid leave of up to 8 weeks. In cases of medical complications, the leave can be extended for an additional 4 weeks with a medical certificate. The leave entitlement cannot be carried forward to the next calendar year and is not cumulative with any other leave. The bank reserves the right to modify the entitlement in line with changes in statutory requirements.

Maternity leave: eligible female employees who have completed a minimum of 12 months of continuous service with the company are entitled to a maximum of 26 weeks (6 months) of maternity leave. The leave may be taken in full or in two consecutive blocks of not less than 12 weeks each. The company shall provide 100% of the employee’s basic salary for the first 90 days of leave. For the remaining period up to 26 weeks, the employee may elect to receive 50% of the basic salary, subject to board approval. Employees are required to submit a medical certificate from a registered practitioner no later than 14 days before the start of leave. Part‑time employees and those on contractual terms are not covered under this policy. In cases of medical complications or pregnancy loss, the employee may apply for an additional 4 weeks of unpaid leave. All maternity leave requests must be submitted at least 30 days prior to the expected due date, and the company reserves the right to postpone the leave for operational reasons.

Eligible female employees who have completed a minimum of twelve months of continuous service are entitled to a total of 26 weeks (182 days) of maternity leave. The leave can be taken as 12 weeks immediately before the expected delivery date and the remaining 14 weeks thereafter, subject to medical certification. The employee will receive 100 % of her basic salary for the first 12 weeks, and thereafter 80 % of the basic salary for the remaining 14 weeks, up to a maximum of Rs. 50,000 per month. The leave is cumulative and can be split into two parts, but not in more than two intervals. Employees in hazardous or high‑risk duties must obtain a medical clearance from a government‑approved physician; if clearance is not granted, the leave may be suspended until the risk is mitigated. Employees who leave the organization before the start of maternity leave lose the entitlement. Adoption and foster care are treated as separate leave under the same terms. Any transfer or change in posting during maternity leave is prohibited, except for essential operational reasons.

Employees who are pregnant and have worked at least 80 days in the 12 months preceding the expected date of delivery are eligible for maternity leave. The leave period is 26 weeks (182 days) in total: the first 12 weeks are paid at 100% of the average daily wage, and the remaining 14 weeks are paid at 50% of that rate. The employee must give the employer a written notice at least 30 days before the expected delivery date, and may claim leave only once in a 12‑month period. Employees who resign, are terminated, or are still on probation are not eligible. For multiple births, an additional 8 weeks of paid leave are granted, making the total 34 weeks. The company also allows a maximum of 3 additional weeks of unpaid leave for personal reasons, subject to managerial approval. Lactation break of up to 2 hours per day is permitted during working hours. Employees who choose to take unpaid leave voluntarily are exempt from the paid leave provisions. All leave claims must be submitted through the HR portal and approved by the line manager. The HR department will review all maternity leave applications and ensure compliance with statutory requirements. Employees may also avail of post‑natal care benefits as per company policy.

Employees who are biological mothers are entitled to maternity leave of 26 weeks (182 days). The first child’s leave is fully paid at 100 % of the employee’s basic salary. For a second child, the company offers 12 weeks (84 days) at 100 % pay; a third child entitles the employee to 6 weeks (42 days) at 100 % pay. Leave can be taken in two blocks, provided the total duration does not exceed the limits above.  

Eligibility: the employee must have worked continuously for the company for at least 12 months and must submit a medical certificate from a licensed physician. Employees on part‑time, contractual or temporary contracts are exempt from paid maternity leave unless they have completed a minimum of 12 months of full‑time work.  

Exceptions: The leave is not applicable to employees who are not biological mothers, to employees who have a pregnancy complication that requires an extended stay beyond the statutory limit (up to an additional 6 weeks at 100 % pay with medical approval), or to employees who have already exhausted the leave for the same child in the current calendar year. Employees who choose to take unpaid leave after the paid period must submit a written request and may be granted up to a maximum of 12 additional weeks at 50 % pay, subject to managerial approval.

Employees who have completed a minimum of 6 months of continuous service and have maintained at least 80 % attendance in the preceding 12 months are eligible for maternity leave. Eligible employees are entitled to a total of 26 weeks (182 days) of leave, of which the first 12 weeks will be paid at 100 % of basic salary, and the remaining 14 weeks at 80 % of basic salary. Employees with a second or subsequent child may take a cumulative total of 26 weeks; however, no single child’s leave may exceed 26 weeks. Unused paid maternity leave can be carried over for a maximum of 2 weeks to the following calendar year.  

All maternity leave must be requested in writing at least 30 days prior to the expected due date, along with a medical certificate. Employees who are on contractual, part‑time, or internship arrangements, or who work in hazardous or high‑risk environments (e.g., manufacturing, construction, or food processing) are exempt from paid maternity leave, though they may be eligible for unpaid leave in accordance with company policy.  

The company will also provide a one‑time 5 % tax‑free maternity benefit for all eligible employees. In case of complications requiring extended hospitalization, employees may apply for additional unpaid medical leave, subject to manager approval.

Employees who become mothers are entitled to a total of 26 weeks (182 days) of maternity leave. The first 12 weeks of leave are paid at 100 % of the employee’s basic salary, and the remaining 14 weeks are paid at 80 % of basic salary, provided the employee’s average monthly earnings during the last 12 months are available. The maximum gratuity payable by the company shall not exceed Rs.20,00,000 (Twenty Lakhs) irrespective of the number of years of service. Employees who retire, resign, or are terminated for reasons other than misconduct are eligible for gratuity; employees terminated for gross misconduct, fraud, or willful disobedience of company policy are not eligible. In the event of death or permanent disablement, the employee’s nominee is entitled to receive the gratuity as per the Act. Gratuity is payable as per the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, subject to company policy. Eligibility: an employee must have completed a minimum of **five (5) consecutive years** of service with the company. The company shall provide a written gratuity certificate upon payment. All gratuity disbursements are subject to the prevailing tax laws and any applicable statutory deductions.

All full‑time employees who have completed a minimum of 180 working days in the current financial year are eligible for the Provident Fund (PF) scheme. The employer and employee each contribute 12 % of the employee’s basic salary (excluding allowances). Contributions are capped at a maximum basic salary of ₹15,000 per month; any amount above this threshold is not considered for PF. For employees whose basic salary falls below ₹10,000, the PF contribution is calculated on the ₹10,000 floor. PF contributions are deposited within 10 days of the end of each month and are automatically deducted from the employee’s salary.

Part‑time, contractual, and internship staff are not covered under the PF scheme unless they are employed on a regular basis for a continuous period of at least 365 days and receive a basic salary of ₹10,000 or more. Employees who have opted for a voluntary retirement plan and those on temporary or short‑term assignments (≤90 days) are exempt. All contributions are governed by the Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952, and the scheme is administered through the local EPFO office. Employees may claim the PF balance upon resignation, retirement, or death, following the standard EPFO claim procedures.

Provident Fund (PF) contributions are mandatory for all regular employees earning a basic salary (including dearness allowance) of ₹15,000 or less per month. The employee contribution is 12 % of the basic salary (plus dearness allowance), while the employer matches 12 % of the same base, subject to a maximum monthly cap of ₹15,000 on each side. Contributions are deducted automatically from the employee’s salary once the employee has completed 60 days of continuous service. Employees who join on a part‑time or contract basis, or who work for the company for less than 60 days, are exempt from PF contributions. Senior management employees whose total monthly remuneration (basic + DA) exceeds ₹15,000 are exempt from the 12 % contribution on the part of the employee, though the employer may still choose to contribute voluntarily. Voluntary Provident Fund (VPF) contributions are permitted up to ₹1,000 per month on top of the statutory contribution. The accumulated balance in the EPF account can be withdrawn after a minimum of five years of service, or earlier in specific circumstances such as medical treatment, marriage, or education. All contributions are remitted to the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) in accordance with prevailing regulations.

All permanent employees whose basic salary is ₹15,000 or less are eligible for the Provident Fund (PF) scheme under the Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952. Eligibility commences on the 30th calendar day of employment. The employee contribution is 12 % of the basic salary (including dearness allowance, if applicable). The employer matches 12 % of the same. The maximum salary subject to PF is ₹15,000; hence, the maximum contribution per month is ₹1,800 from each side. Employees earning above ₹15,000 are exempt from PF contributions; instead, the company will offer a Voluntary Provident Fund (VPF) of up to 12 % of the basic salary. Contractual, temporary, and part‑time employees are not covered by the statutory PF; they may opt for a voluntary scheme. Employees on medical leave or unpaid leave are exempt from contributions for the leave period. All contributions are deducted and remitted to the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) by the 15th of each month.

All regular employees earning a basic salary of ₹50,000 or more per month are eligible to contribute to the Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF). Contributions are calculated as 12 % of the employee’s basic pay plus dearness allowance, matched by the employer at 12 % of the same base. The EPF contribution is deducted on the 25th day of every month, and the total annual contribution (employee + employer) shall not exceed ₹18,000. Employees who have completed less than 180 days of continuous service in the current financial year are excluded from automatic deduction; they may opt in upon meeting the 180‑day threshold. Contract staff earning a fixed monthly rate above ₹1,50,000 are exempt, but they can voluntarily contribute up to the statutory limit. Employees on maternity leave will continue to receive employer contributions even if salary is paused. Any employee with a gross salary exceeding ₹20,00,000 per month is ineligible for EPF and will be directed to the Employees’ Pension Scheme. Contributions are reviewed quarterly; any discrepancy is corrected within the following month.

Employees who have completed at least 30 consecutive days of service and whose basic salary (excluding allowances) is not less than ₹5,000 per month are eligible for the Provident Fund (PF). The employer and employee shall each contribute 12% of the basic salary. The maximum contribution per month is capped at ₹10,000. In case of senior officials (designation level 6 and above) and Special Category Employees, the contribution rate is 14% of basic salary, with the same monthly cap of ₹10,000. For employees with a basic salary exceeding ₹50,000, the contribution shall be calculated on the salary up to ₹50,000; any amount above this threshold is exempt from PF contributions. Part‑time and contractual staff who work for less than 120 days in a fiscal year are exempt from PF contributions unless they opt in, in which case the contribution is prorated based on days worked. Employees on medical leave or maternity leave are still counted as eligible for PF contributions, provided they are physically present for at least 90 days during the fiscal year. The contributions are deposited monthly, and any shortfall due to salary variations shall be adjusted in the subsequent month.

Provident Fund (PF) Contribution: All full‑time employees earning up to ₹15,000 per month are required to contribute 12% of their basic salary and dearness allowance. The employer matches the same 12%. The maximum contribution per month is capped at ₹15,000, which is the current ceiling set by the Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952. Employees who have worked a minimum of 60 days in a financial year are eligible for PF benefits. New hires on probation are eligible after completing 30 consecutive days of employment. Casual, contract and part‑time staff, as well as interns and trainees, are exempt from PF contributions. Employees earning above ₹15,000 per month may opt into the scheme on a voluntary basis; if opted, the contribution remains 12% of the capped ₹15,000. All contributions are remitted to the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) within the statutory deadline, and the hospital maintains a record of contributions for each employee. Employees who leave the organization after 24 months of continuous service are eligible to claim the accumulated PF balance, subject to standard EPFO rules.

Employees who earn a monthly salary up to ₹21,000 (current ESI limit) and who are employed for a minimum of 7 days in a month are eligible for ESI benefits. The bank’s contribution is 4.75 % of the employee’s gross wages; the employee contributes 1.75 %. An additional 0.75 % is paid by the bank to cover the medical component, making the total contribution 6.25 %. Contributions are capped at the wage ceiling of ₹21,000, so no employee with wages above this limit is required to pay the employee share, but the employer still pays the full 4.75 % on the capped amount.  

Eligible employees receive:  
• Sickness benefit: 90 % of the average daily wages for 90 consecutive days, up to a maximum of ₹20,000 per month.  
• Maternity benefit: 100 % of wages for 12 weeks (including 8 weeks paid at 100 % and 4 weeks at 50 % for those with less than 12 months’ service).  
• Dependents’ sickness benefit: 90 % of wages for 60 days.  

Exceptions:  
• Contractual and part‑time employees are not covered unless they meet the minimum 7‑day employment requirement.  
• Employees earning above ₹21,000 are exempt from employee contributions but remain eligible for the employer’s share if they voluntarily opt into the scheme.  
• Employees who terminate employment before completing 7 days are not eligible for any benefit.

All full‑time retail employees earning a monthly wage of ₹21,000 or less are covered under the Employees’ State Insurance (ESI) Scheme. Coverage begins after 30 consecutive days of employment and requires a minimum of 20 working hours per week. The employer contributes 4.75 % of the employee’s wages (up to ₹21,000), while the employee contributes 1.75 % toward the scheme.  

ESI benefits include:  
• **Sickness benefits** – up to ₹15,000 for 91 days of sickness per year, payable after 15 days of medical certification.  
• **Maternity benefits** – ₹15,000 for 26 weeks, available to female employees after 90 days of employment.  
• **Disabled and dependent benefits** – up to ₹15,000 for permanent disability and ₹5,000 for dependent children per annum.  

Employees on temporary, seasonal, or contractual arrangements, and those earning above ₹21,000 per month, are exempt from ESI coverage. All benefits are subject to the national ESI Act limits and can be accessed through the company’s designated ESI portal. The company will provide ESI insurance certificates upon completion of the 30‑day probation period.

The insurance premium is shared 3.25 % of the employee’s wages, with the employer contributing 4.75 % and the employee contributing 0.75 %. The scheme provides a 100 % cash benefit for maternity up to 100 days, and a cashless benefit for sickness, maternity, and pre‑ and post‑natal care up to ₹1 lakh per annum. In case of accidental death, the dependent receives a lump‑sum payment of ₹10 lakh. Workers who have worked fewer than 20 days or earn above the ₹21,000 threshold are excluded, but may opt for voluntary coverage at a higher rate. Contractual, casual and temporary staff are not covered unless they meet the monthly wage and attendance criteria. Employees falling under the Employees’ State Insurance Act, 1948, are eligible for a comprehensive welfare package. The scheme provides 100 % wage replacement for sickness up to 18 months, 30 % wage replacement for maternity up to 26 weeks, 50 % replacement for permanent disability, and full replacement for temporary disability. Medical benefits include free inpatient care up to ₹3 lakh per year and free outpatient care up to 20 visits per year. Employees earning ₹21 000 or less per month and working a minimum of 20 days in a month are covered; those earning above this threshold or engaged in non-regular employment are exempt. Employees who leave the organization before completing 60 days of service are not eligible for any benefits. Employer and employee contributions are 4.75 % and 1.75 % of wages, respectively, subject to a ceiling of ₹21 000 per month. The scheme does not cover casual, contract, or temporary staff. In case of a qualifying event, employees must file a claim within 30 days; delayed claims are forfeited. The HR department will verify eligibility and facilitate all claim processes.

Employees earning a monthly wage up to ₹21,000 and working a minimum of 30 days in any calendar month are eligible for ESI coverage. The employer contributes 4.75 % of the employee’s wages and the employee contributes 1.75 % for a total of 6.50 % of wages. Contributions are calculated on the actual wages earned, including overtime, allowances and bonuses, up to the prescribed ceiling of ₹21,000. ESI entitles employees to a cash benefit of ₹1,200 for sickness up to 180 days, and a cash benefit of ₹5,400 for maternity up to 45 days. Medical benefit covers hospitalization up to 90 days with a maximum of ₹10,000 per case, and outpatient treatment up to ₹2,000 per year. Employees who are casual, contract or part‑time and work less than 30 days are excluded from coverage. In addition, employees earning above ₹21,000 are exempt from ESI, but may opt for voluntary ESI under the company’s scheme. All claims must be submitted within 30 days of the event and accompanied by the required medical certificates.

Employees who earn a monthly wage of ₹21,000 or less and work a minimum of 20 hours per week are eligible for the Employees’ State Insurance (ESI) scheme. Under this scheme, the employer contributes 4.75% of the employee’s wages, while the employee contributes 1.75%, both capped at the statutory limit of ₹21,000 per month. The insurance covers up to 100% of the employee’s wages for medical treatment, with a maximum benefit of ₹1,500 per month per person. Sickness benefits are payable for up to 90 consecutive days at 80% of the average daily wage, and maternity benefits are granted for 100 days (120 days if the employee has a disability) at 100% of the average daily wage. Dependents (spouse and children under 18) receive the same benefit coverage as the employee.  

Exceptions: employees earning above ₹21,000, contract workers, casual staff working less than 20 hours a week, and those employed in temporary or seasonal positions are not covered. Employees who voluntarily opt out of ESI, after giving a written notice of 30 days, are exempted but will lose coverage. The company will submit monthly payroll reports to the ESI authorities to ensure compliance.

All employees earning a gross monthly wage of ₹21,000 or less are covered under the Employee State Insurance (ESI) Scheme, effective from the first day of their employment. The Employer contributes 4.75% and the Employee contributes 0.75% of the total wages (capped at ₹21,000) to the ESI fund. Coverage is applicable only to those who work a minimum of 30 days in a calendar year and are on a full‑time roster. Casual, contract, and freelance workers, as well as employees earning above ₹21,000, are exempt from ESI.  

The benefits under ESI are:  
• **Sickness benefit** – 100 % wage replacement for up to 180 consecutive days, with a maximum monthly benefit of ₹14,400.  
• **Maternity benefit** – 90 days for the first child and 90 days for subsequent children, with a maximum monthly benefit of ₹14,400.  
• **Medical benefit** – free treatment for the employee and dependents up to ₹5,000 per month.  

If an employee’s wage exceeds ₹21,000 after 12 consecutive months, they will automatically be deregistered from ESI, and no contributions will be made thereafter. Employees may apply for re‑registration if their wage falls back below the threshold.

text: Employees eligible for work‑from‑home (WFH) are those in permanent, full‑time roles with a minimum of 6 months tenure, holding a regular or higher grade as per the company’s grading system. Each eligible employee may work from home up to 2 days per week, not exceeding 8 hours per day, and the total WFH hours must not surpass 70 % of the monthly work hours (≈ 120 hours for a 40‑hour work week). WFH is allowed only on days when the employee’s functional responsibilities can be fulfilled remotely and no client‑specific on‑site requirement is in place. Managers must obtain prior approval for WFH days via the internal portal; approvals are granted by the employee’s immediate supervisor and the HR Business Partner. Exceptions include: (i) employees in client‑facing roles with active on‑site contracts, (ii) roles requiring physical equipment or presence, (iii) periods of public health or natural disaster where office access is impossible, and (iv) emergency situations requiring immediate on‑site presence. The company reserves the right to revoke WFH privileges if performance or compliance with security protocols deteriorates. All WFH arrangements are governed by the company’s Information Security and Data Privacy guidelines.

Employees who have completed a minimum of six months of continuous service and hold a position that can be performed remotely are eligible to work from home (WFH) up to three days per calendar week, subject to managerial approval. The WFH allowance is capped at 70% of the employee’s total scheduled working hours per month (i.e. 15 hours per week for a 20‑hour work week). Any additional hours beyond the prescribed limit must be logged and approved separately. Employees in field‑based, supervisory or client‑interaction roles are ineligible for WFH unless a role‑specific exemption is granted by the HR Director after a performance review. During periods of national emergency, public health crisis or unavoidable personal hardship, employees may request up to five consecutive WFH days per month, which will be considered on a case‑by‑case basis. All WFH employees must have a reliable internet connection, access to the NGO’s VPN, and be available for virtual meetings from 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM IST. The organization will provide a one‑time laptop stipend of ₹15,000 and a monthly data allowance of ₹2,000, subject to receipt of a signed equipment usage agreement. Non‑compliance with the stated availability or security protocols will result in revocation of WFH privileges.

Work from home (WFH) is allowed for eligible employees in non‑front‑line roles. Eligibility requires a minimum of 6 months continuous service, no outstanding performance or disciplinary actions, and a role that can be performed remotely. Employees may work from home up to two (2) days per week, with a maximum of 40 % of their total working hours (i.e., 32 hours in an 8‑hour day). The total number of WFH days in a calendar year is capped at 12. Managers must approve each WFH request in advance and ensure that the employee has a suitable workspace and reliable internet. WFH cannot exceed 3 consecutive days and at any given time no more than 10 % of the workforce can be remote to maintain store operations. Sales and customer‑support staff may apply for WFH on a case‑by‑case basis if it does not interfere with client visits. All remote work must comply with the company’s data‑security guidelines and employees must submit a weekly activity log for audit.

Employees who have completed a minimum of 12 months in the bank and are in roles that do not require physical presence at a branch or data centre are eligible for a Work‑From‑Home (WFH) arrangement. Under the policy an employee may work remotely up to **2 days per week** (maximum **8 days per month**) provided that they maintain a minimum of **60 %** of their total contractual working days on site. Requests for additional WFH days must be submitted at least **7 days in advance** and approved by the employee’s immediate manager and HR.  

The policy allows a one‑time **trial period of 4 weeks** for new hires (first‑year employees) to assess suitability. WFH is not permitted for positions in the **Information Technology**, **Risk Management**, or **Retail Operations** teams where data security or customer interaction is mandatory. Employees who exceed the monthly limit of **8 WFH days** in a single month will be subject to a review and may be required to return to the office. The bank will provide a dedicated laptop and will cover up to **₹4,000 per month** for internet usage. All employees must adhere to the bank’s data‑protection guidelines and report any technical or security incidents within **24 hours**.

Employees in non‑clinical departments who have no direct patient‑contact responsibilities are eligible to work from home for up to two days per month, provided they maintain an 80 % online presence and are reachable during core hours (09:00–18:00 IST). Eligible staff include administrators, finance, human resources, IT, research and policy teams, and all permanent full‑time employees. Contractual and part‑time staff may request up to one remote day per month, subject to manager approval. Employees must not exceed 16 hours of continuous work and must submit a daily log via the intranet portal. Work‑from‑home days are capped at two consecutive days; any additional remote work requires a written justification and approval from the HR head. Exceptions are granted for medical or personal emergencies, and for roles that involve remote monitoring or tele‑consultation, where 100 % remote work is permissible. The hospital reserves the right to revoke or modify remote‑work entitlements if performance or security concerns arise.

Employees who have completed a minimum of 12 months of continuous service and have consistently met or exceeded performance targets for the last six months are eligible for the Work‑From‑Home (WFH) program. Each employee may work from home up to 3 days per week (maximum 12 days per month) provided that core business hours (9:00 am–12:30 pm, 2:30 pm–6:30 pm) are covered by at least one in‑office staff member. The total number of WFH days per year cannot exceed 48 days. WFH requests must be submitted at least 48 hours in advance using the internal portal and are subject to manager approval. Employees in roles that require real‑time customer interaction (e.g., Tier‑1 support) are ineligible for WFH unless an approved exception is granted by the Operations Director. Temporary WFH arrangements may be granted for medical or personal emergencies, up to a maximum of 10 consecutive days, with documentation required. All WFH employees must maintain a stable broadband connection, ensure a distraction‑free workspace, and report daily attendance via the company app. Failure to comply may result in revocation of WFH privileges.

Work‑From‑Home (WFH) Policy  
All employees who have completed a minimum of 12 months continuous service and hold non‑safety‑critical, non‑patient‑direct roles are eligible to apply for WFH. Each eligible employee may work from home up to 3 days per week (maximum 12 days in a 30‑day month). The WFH arrangement is subject to a 30 % workforce cap per department to ensure adequate on‑site presence. Employees may not exceed 60 % of their total contractual working days per fiscal year in WFH.  

Core‑hours policy: employees must be available online from 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM IST for virtual meetings and collaboration. All WFH work must comply with the company’s Information Security and Data Protection guidelines; personal devices must have approved VPN and anti‑virus software.  

Exceptions:  
• Senior management, project leads, and remote‑service roles may request up to 5 WFH days per week, subject to managerial approval.  
• Employees in R&D, compliance, or regulatory affairs with critical in‑lab responsibilities may be restricted to on‑site presence only.  
• During emergency situations (e.g., natural disasters, public health crises) the WFH limit may be temporarily increased upon notification by the HR Director.  

All WFH requests must be submitted through the internal portal and approved by the employee’s supervisor and HR within 5 business days. Failure to adhere to the core‑hours or security requirements may result in revocation of WFH privileges.

Employees may work from home (WFH) for a maximum of 2 days per week, provided that the total remote working hours do not exceed 20 % of the contractual monthly hours (i.e. 16 hours per month for a 40‑hour work week). Eligibility requires: (i) full‑time status, (ii) a minimum tenure of 6 months, (iii) a performance rating of at least “satisfactory” in the last appraisal cycle, and (iv) job functions that can be performed remotely (e.g., software development, data analysis, design). Managers must approve WFH requests in writing at least 48 hours before the scheduled day.

Exceptions: (a) Roles that mandate on‑site presence (e.g., product testing, manufacturing, client‑facing sales, on‑site support) are ineligible for WFH. (b) Critical periods such as product launches, major deliverables, or client deadlines may restrict WFH, with a maximum of 1 WFH day per month during these periods. (c) Employees with a history of non‑compliance or unsatisfactory performance may be denied WFH. All WFH arrangements are reviewed quarterly; repeated violations may lead to revocation of WFH privileges.

Eligible employees must be on a full‑time contract, have completed at least one year of service, and have no disciplinary action in the last 12 months. Work‑from‑home (WFH) is permitted for up to **three (3) days per week**, with a **maximum of twelve (12) WFH days per calendar month**. Requests must be submitted to the immediate supervisor at least **48 hours in advance** and approved by the department head. The WFH schedule must not exceed **30 % of the employee’s total working days** in a fiscal year. The company will ensure that no more than **10 % of the workforce is onsite at any given time** to maintain operational continuity.  

Employees must maintain a dedicated workspace, secure Wi‑Fi with a minimum speed of **20 Mbps**, and comply with data‑protection protocols, including the use of company‑issued VPN and two‑factor authentication. All WFH days must be logged in the HR portal; employees working more than six (6) hours must record their start and end times.  

Exceptions are granted for medical reasons, family emergencies, or special project requirements, subject to manager approval. Employees on leave, sick, or undergoing training are not eligible for WFH during those periods.

Attendance and punctuality are critical to maintaining service quality. Employees are expected to report to their assigned shift at least 10 minutes before the scheduled start time. Late arrivals are counted as a "late" if the employee arrives more than 10 minutes after the scheduled shift start. Each month, a maximum of 3 late incidents is allowed. Accumulation of 5 or more late incidents in any calendar month will result in a written warning. An employee with 3 consecutive months of zero or one late incident will be eligible for a "Late‑free" certificate, which may be considered during performance reviews. Attendance is recorded in the company system; manual adjustments are permitted only after submission of a valid medical certificate or a written apology in cases of unforeseen personal emergencies. Employees on a flexible schedule or working from home must notify their supervisor at least 24 hours prior to any deviation from the agreed hours. Exceptions are granted for unavoidable circumstances such as extreme weather, public transport strikes, or medical emergencies. Repeated violations beyond the stipulated limits may lead to progressive disciplinary action, up to termination.

Attendance and punctuality are essential to the smooth operation of our manufacturing plant. All full‑time employees are required to achieve a minimum attendance rate of 95 % in any calendar month, calculated as (days present ÷ 20 working days) × 100. Late arrivals are counted when an employee clocks in more than 10 minutes after the scheduled start time (08:30 hrs). A single late arrival is noted as 0.5 % of the monthly attendance rate; two late arrivals in a month are considered 1 %. Accumulating three or more late arrivals within a month will trigger a warning, and four or more will result in a deduction of one day’s wages, subject to the company’s grievance procedure. 

Employees on probation are exempt from the 95 % attendance requirement until the end of their probationary period, after which the same rules apply. Part‑time and contract workers are evaluated on a pro‑rated basis and are not subject to wage deductions, but repeated lateness will lead to contract review. 

Allowed exceptions include: (i) medical appointments with a doctor’s note, (ii) emergencies affecting the employee or immediate family, (iii) public holidays and official non‑working days, and (iv) documented transport disruptions. All exceptions must be reported to the supervisor within one hour of the scheduled start time and verified with supporting documentation.

Full‑time employees are expected to clock in within 15 minutes of their scheduled start time. Any entry beyond this window is recorded as a tardy. A maximum of 5 tardies per month is permissible. Accumulating more than 5 tardies in a calendar month will trigger a deduction of one paid leave day for each additional tardy beyond the 5th. Employees are allowed a maximum of 3 unexcused absences per quarter. Exceeding 3 absences within the same quarter will result in a review by HR and possible disciplinary action. Attendance is measured on a rolling 30‑day basis, and a cumulative absence rate of over 10% within any 3‑month period will prompt a performance discussion. Eligible employees include all regular full‑time staff; interns, contract workers, and part‑time staff are excluded from this attendance calculation. Exceptions are granted for medically certified illnesses, pregnancy, or bereavement, provided a doctor’s note or official documentation is submitted within 48 hours. Work‑from‑home days and company‑approved leave are recorded as attended and do not count towards tardies or absences.

Employees are expected to report to their assigned store at least 30 minutes before the official shift start time. An employee is considered late if they arrive after the scheduled start time minus the 30‑minute grace period. For full‑time staff, a single late arrival is recorded as a 5% attendance penalty.
