All regular full‑time employees must be present by 9:30 am. A 5‑minute grace period is allowed; lateness beyond 9:35 am is recorded as a “late” day. The first three late days in a calendar month incur no penalty. From the fourth late day onwards, 2 % of the employee’s gross monthly salary is deducted per late day. Attendance is tracked via the company’s HRIS; each day of absence without prior approval is treated as a missed day. Employees must achieve a minimum of 22 working days per month; falling below 20 days triggers a formal warning.  

Eligibility: The policy applies to all regular full‑time staff. Contract, internship, and freelance personnel are governed by separate terms. Exceptions: A medical certificate or a police report for a sudden emergency allows up to 3 days of unexcused lateness or absence without penalty per fiscal year. Approved work‑from‑home or flexible‑shift arrangements are exempt from lateness penalties if logged correctly.

This policy governs attendance and punctuality for all employees of XYZ Hospital. Employees are required to be present and on time for their scheduled shift. An employee is considered “late” if they arrive more than 15 minutes after the scheduled start time. A maximum of three (3) late arrivals per month is permitted. On the fourth late arrival in any calendar month, a deduction of 5 % of that day’s basic salary will be applied. If an employee accumulates five (5) or more late arrivals in a quarter, a written warning will be issued and the employee will be placed on a performance improvement plan. Absences without prior approval are counted as unexcused absences. A maximum of two (2) unexcused absences per month is allowed; exceeding this limit will result in a reduction of attendance bonus

Employees are expected to be present at their assigned post for the full scheduled working day. The bank operates 22 working days a month. Attendance is calculated on a 100% basis for every scheduled day. Late arrivals are classified as follows: arrival within 15 minutes of the scheduled start time is excused; arrival between 15–30 minutes is considered a ‘late’ and will be recorded; arrival between 30–60 minutes is a ‘partial’ late and will be recorded as 0.5 day absent; arrival after 60 minutes is treated as an unexcused absence. An employee may have no more than five late records (15–30 min) in a calendar month. Exceeding this threshold triggers a 1 % deduction of the employee’s basic salary per late occurrence. Attendance records are reviewed monthly; any discrepancy must be reported within 48 hours. Eligibility for attendance benefits applies only to employees who have completed a 6‑month probationary period. Valid medical certificates, approved leave, official business travel, or unavoidable emergencies are exempt from late‑arrival or absentee penalties. All exceptions must be documented in the employee’s attendance register and approved by the HR manager.

Attendance and Late Coming Policy

Employees are required to maintain a minimum attendance of 95 % in a fiscal year, calculated on all working days excluding statutory holidays and approved leaves. Unexcused absences exceeding 5 % of scheduled working days (e.g., more than 18 days in a 365‑day year) will trigger a written warning. Late arrivals are permitted up to 15 minutes after the official start time. Accumulation of more than 3 % late arrivals (e.g., 11 or more late days in a 365‑day year) will result in a formal reprimand and may affect performance appraisal.

Full‑time, part‑time, and contract staff are covered by this policy. Internship and training staff are exempt from the 95 % attendance requirement but must adhere to a 90 % minimum for training periods. Employees on approved medical or family emergencies, official duty, or natural disaster relief are granted excused absences, provided proper documentation is submitted within 48 hours.

Employees must report lateness or absence to their immediate supervisor and HR within 30 minutes of arrival or departure. Unexcused absences or lateness beyond the stated limits may lead to deduction of leave days, suspension, or termination in accordance with the PSU's disciplinary procedures.

Attendance is mandatory for all full‑time staff, interns, and contractual employees of the NGO. Each employee is allowed a maximum of 3 unexcused absences per calendar month. Late arrivals are permitted up to 10 minutes beyond the scheduled start time; any lateness exceeding 10 minutes is counted as an unexcused absence. Cumulative unexcused absences exceeding 5 days in a rolling 12‑month period will trigger a formal warning. For part‑time staff and volunteers, a maximum of 5 unexcused absences per year is permissible. All absences must be reported to the HR desk within 30 minutes of arrival or by the end of the day if the employee is already present. Eligible reasons for excused absences include documented medical certificates, official government notifications, or bereavement (up to 3 consecutive days). Short‑term illnesses (≤2 days) are considered excused without documentation if the employee informs the supervisor in advance. Exceptions for natural disasters, public transport strikes, or unforeseen emergencies are granted on a case‑by‑case basis, provided the employee supplies a brief written explanation within 48 hours. Persistent non‑compliance may lead to suspension or termination following the NGO’s grievance procedure.

Employees who work beyond the regular 8‑hour workday are eligible for overtime compensation, provided they are in a permanent or contractual employment relationship (interns, volunteers and trainees are excluded). Overtime is paid at 1.5 × the normal hourly rate for the first 10 hours worked in a day, and at 2 × for any additional hours beyond 10 in that same day. The total overtime payable in a calendar month shall not exceed 20 days of overtime work, and the cumulative overtime hours in a year shall not surpass 200 hours. The maximum overtime payment for a month is capped at 10 % of the employee’s basic monthly salary. Overtime approval must be obtained in advance from the immediate supervisor, unless the overtime is necessary for emergency operations (e.g., medical emergencies, critical event management) in which case a post‑event approval from the HR manager is sufficient. The policy does not apply to employees in the finance or administration departments who are working on a fixed‑hourly basis; they are covered under the organization’s standard pay structure.

All non-executive employees who work beyond their scheduled hours are eligible for overtime compensation. Overtime is calculated at 1.5 times the employee’s basic hourly rate for the first 20 hours per month and at 2.0 times for any hours beyond that. The total overtime payable per month cannot exceed 10% of the employee’s basic monthly salary. Employees may accrue a maximum of 30 overtime days in a fiscal year; any excess must be converted to leave without pay. Approval for overtime must be obtained in writing from the immediate supervisor and recorded in the bank’s time‑keeping system. Overtime is not payable for duties performed on statutory holidays, national holidays, or in compliance with regulatory mandates such as RBI’s “Night Shift” rule for treasury operations. Senior management, fixed‑scheduling staff, and outsourced contractors are exempt from this policy unless they sign a separate overtime agreement. Unapproved overtime is treated as a breach of the bank’s code of conduct and may result in disciplinary action.

Employees who work beyond the scheduled 8‑hour day or exceed 10 hours in a working week are eligible for overtime. Overtime shall be compensated at a rate of 1.5 × basic hourly wage, capped at a maximum of 2 overtime hours per day and 10 overtime hours per week. The total overtime payment for a month shall not exceed INR 25,000 per employee. Only regular, full‑time staff (excluding temporary or contractual workers) may claim overtime. Prior written approval from the shift supervisor is required for each overtime session; unapproved overtime will be treated as normal working hours and will not be paid. Overtime is not payable for night duty (10 pm–6 am) unless the employee works beyond the normal night shift hours of 8 hours, in which case the same 1.5× rate applies. Exceptions apply only in cases of plant shutdown, emergency repairs, or safety‑critical operations, and must be documented by the plant manager and approved by HR. All overtime must be logged in the company’s time‑keeping system, and payroll will reflect the overtime payment on the next bi‑weekly pay cycle.

Overtime is permitted for eligible regular employees working beyond the standard 8‑hour day or 48‑hour week, subject to prior approval by the Shift Manager or Store Manager. Overtime shall be compensated at 1.5 × the employee’s basic hourly rate for the first 2 hours on any day, and 2 × for any additional hours on the same day. The maximum payable overtime per day is 4 hours and per week is 12 hours; any overtime exceeding these limits requires written authorization from the Regional HR Office and may be reimbursed as a one‑time allowance instead of salary. Overtime is applicable only on weekdays (Monday–Saturday) and is not automatically granted on Sundays or company holidays unless pre‑approved. Managers, executive staff, and employees engaged in fixed shift rotation (e.g., 12‑hour night shifts) are exempt from overtime calculation and receive a fixed premium instead. All overtime must be logged in the company’s time‑keeping system and paid in the following month’s salary. The company strictly adheres to the Employees’ Compensation Act, 1923, ensuring overtime pay never falls below 1.5 × basic salary. For queries, contact the HR Helpdesk at hr@retailchain.in.

Overtime shall be paid for any hours worked beyond the scheduled 8 hours per day or 48 hours per week, provided such work is approved in advance by the shift supervisor. Eligible employees include all clinical and non‑clinical staff who are not classified as exempt under the Payment of Wages Act. Exempt personnel—chief physicians, senior managers, and directors—are not entitled to overtime compensation.

The overtime rate is 1.5 × basic hourly wage for the first 3 hours each day and 2.0 × basic for any additional hours, up to a maximum of 20 overtime hours per month. Overtime cannot exceed 60 % of the employee’s basic monthly salary. Emergency duty, on‑call rotations, or night shifts that are part of the regular roster are excluded from overtime calculations.

All overtime claims must be recorded on the hospital’s time‑keeping system and submitted within 7 days of the end of the shift. Payment will be made in the subsequent payroll cycle, no later than 30 days after the month ends. Violations of this policy may result in disciplinary action.

Employees who work beyond the statutory 8‑hour workday or 48‑hour workweek are entitled to overtime compensation. Overtime is calculated at 1.5× the normal hourly rate for the first 2 hours beyond the standard day and 2× for any additional hour. For Sundays and public holidays, the overtime rate is 3× the regular hourly rate. An employee may record a maximum of 20 overtime days per calendar month; exceeding this limit requires prior written approval from the manager.  

Eligibility: all regular full‑time employees, contract employees after a 3‑month probationary period, and part‑time employees with a signed overtime agreement. Interns, trainees and employees on a fixed‑term project contract are excluded unless a special clause is added to their contract.  

Exceptions: (i) emergency or critical incident response where overtime is performed after 10 pm; (ii) project deadlines that have been formally approved; (iii) employees who elect to work overtime without remuneration under a signed waiver.  

Overtime payment is processed within 15 days of the month

Overtime shall be paid to eligible permanent employees only. An employee is eligible for overtime when the total hours worked in a working day exceed eight (8) hours, provided that such overtime is not more than twenty‑four (24) hours in any contiguous seven (7) day period. Overtime compensation is calculated on the basis of the basic hourly rate (Basic Salary ÷ 2,080 hours). The rate is 1.5 times the basic hourly rate for the first two (2) overtime hours of the day, and 2.0 times the basic hourly rate for any additional overtime hours beyond the first two. The maximum overtime payable in a calendar month is capped at 120 hours. Overtime worked on a public holiday or during a declared emergency is exempt from the 24‑hour weekly limit but must be recorded in a timesheet and approved by the immediate supervisor within 48 hours. Supervisory and managerial staff may exceed the 24‑hour limit only with prior written approval from the HR Manager, and such overtime must be justified by a project charter or critical operational requirement. All overtime must be submitted through the electronic time‑tracking system for payroll processing.

Overtime is defined as any work beyond the standard 9 AM–6 PM, 8‑hour shift. Approved overtime is payable at 1.25× the basic hourly rate on weekdays and 1.50× on Saturdays and Sundays. Employees may work a maximum of 20 overtime hours per month; any hours beyond 20 are converted into paid leave. Overtime must be pre‑approved by the employee’s manager and logged in the company time‑sheet system. Eligibility: full‑time staff who have completed the 3‑month probation period; interns, contractors and freelance staff are exempt. Special cases: if overtime exceeds 10 hours in a single week, the company must compensate the employee within 48 hours. Public holidays: if work is required, overtime is paid at 2.5× the normal rate, and the employee must receive a compensatory day off. Employees may not work overtime on Sundays unless an emergency arises, in which case the same 2.5× rate applies. Any overtime exceeding 8 consecutive working days must be reported, and the employee will be granted a mandatory rest period of 48 hours. The policy applies only to in‑office work; remote work overtime follows the same rules but is logged via the company portal.

Overtime is compensated only when prior written approval is obtained from the shift manager. Full‑time employees who work beyond the scheduled 8‑hour shift are eligible for overtime pay. The first 2 hours of overtime each working day are paid at 1.25 × the basic hourly rate. Any overtime beyond 2 hours in the same day is paid at 1.5 × the basic hourly rate. Overtime shall not exceed 40 hours per calendar month or 10 hours in any consecutive 7‑day period. The maximum payable overtime per month is capped at 200 % of the employee’s basic monthly salary, whichever is lower. Employees on the 6‑day work week (Monday‑Saturday) are eligible for overtime on any of those days, but not on Sundays unless it is an emergency call or scheduled night shift. Contractual and outsourced staff are excluded from overtime eligibility unless expressly stated in their agreement. Employees who exceed the monthly limit will receive the excess hours as compensatory leave, to be used within 30 days from the end of the month.

Overtime is payable to regular employees who work beyond the standard 8‑hour workday or 48‑hour workweek. Eligible employees are those on a full‑time contract and have completed a probation period of 3 months. Overtime is compensated at 1.5× the employee’s basic hourly rate for weekday hours (Monday‑Friday) and 2× for weekend or public holiday hours. The company limits overtime to a maximum of 20 hours per calendar month; any hours beyond this threshold will be treated as unpaid overtime unless prior written approval is obtained from the department head. Overtime is calculated on a per‑day basis, with a maximum of 2 hours per day permissible under normal circumstances. Exceptions apply for critical production or emergency situations where overtime may be authorized up to 4 hours per day without a prior approval, but such overtime must be recorded and submitted for audit within 48 hours. Contract‑based and temporary staff are excluded from overtime pay unless their contract specifically states otherwise. All overtime must be logged in the timesheet system and approved by the immediate supervisor before payment.

Employees receive their gross salary every month on the 5th of the month, calculated as Basic (20% of CTC) + DA (8% of Basic), HRA (40% of Basic), and other allowances. The net salary is computed after statutory deductions: Provident Fund 12% of Basic, Professional Tax up to ₹200 per month, and applicable income tax per slab. The payslip is emailed electronically and also available in hard copy at the HR office within 48 hours of salary credit. Eligibility for salary payment requires a signed Employment Agreement and completion of probation (first 3 months). Part‑time staff are paid pro‑rated on days worked, capped at 20 days per month. Interns receive stipend of ₹15,000/month, exempt from PF but subject to TDS. Employees on extended maternity leave (up to 6 weeks) receive 80% of basic salary; on medical leave exceeding 14 days, 70% of basic is paid. Salary adjustments are processed only during the annual review cycle and after performance appraisal.

Employees shall receive their gross monthly salary in a single direct deposit no later than 7 calendar days after the last working day of the month. The payslip, detailing gross pay, statutory deductions (e.g., EPF 12%, ESIC 4.75%, professional tax up to ₹200, income tax as per slab), and net pay, will be emailed within 5 calendar days of the salary credit. Eligibility: all full‑time employees with a valid employment contract are entitled to salary. Contractual part‑time staff earning less than ₹20,000 per month are paid bi‑weekly and receive a simplified payslip. Remote employees based outside India are paid via international wire, with the same 7‑day window, and must provide a valid bank account. Exceptions: Employees on unpaid leave, interns, or temporary contract staff will receive a pro‑rated salary; however, payslips for interns are not required unless the internship is longer than 3 months. Salary caps: no employee’s basic salary will exceed ₹10,00,000 per annum without board approval. Salary adjustments are reviewed quarterly, and any increase must be reflected in the next payslip.

Salary payment and payslip

All permanent employees receive their salary on the 25th of each month. The payslip must be issued electronically within five (5) working days of the salary credit. Employees whose gross monthly salary exceeds ₹1,00,000 are eligible for a performance bonus of up to 15% of their base salary, payable in the next month’s pay slip, subject to board approval.

Overtime is compensated at 1.5 times the basic rate for the first 20 hours per month and 2.0 times thereafter. Any deduction beyond 10% of the gross salary in a month, including salary advance, loans, or tax withholding, must receive written consent from the employee. Employees on probation (first 3 months) are exempt from the bonus and overtime payout until the probation period is successfully completed.

Contractual staff, interns, and freelancers are not eligible for monthly salary benefits and will receive payments on a per‑project basis as per their agreement. Employees who have resigned or been terminated will receive the outstanding salary within 30 days of the last working day, subject to settlement of all dues.

All salaries will be credited to employees’ designated bank accounts on or before the 5th working day of each month, following the statutory payroll cycle of 30 calendar days from the date of salary approval. Employees will receive a detailed payslip by 8:00 AM on the 5th day, which includes gross salary, basic, HRA, special allowances, and statutory deductions such as PF (12% of basic), EPF (8% of basic), and professional tax as per state norms. Net salary will be calculated after deducting taxes, loan EMIs, and any other authorized deductions, with a maximum voluntary deduction capped at 25% of the gross salary per month.

Salary revisions are approved annually on the employee’s anniversary of joining and may be adjusted mid‑year for performance or cost‑of‑living adjustments, but the increase cannot exceed 10% of the current base salary in any single year. Employees on a fixed‑term contract or temporary status are exempt from annual salary reviews unless their contract is extended. Interns, part‑time staff, and employees on leave of absence do not receive a payslip or salary unless a written agreement states otherwise. Any deviation from the stated limits or dates requires written approval from the HR head and the finance director.

Salary and Payslip  

1. Salary will be credited to the employee’s bank account on the 30th day of each calendar month.  
2. An electronic payslip will be generated and available on the PSU intranet portal no later than the 5th day of the following month.  
3. Deductions:  
   – Professional Tax: 5% of basic salary, capped at ₹2,500 per month.  
   – Provident Fund (Employee Contribution): 12% of basic salary, capped at ₹25,200 per annum (₹2,100 per month).  
   – Income Tax: As per applicable slab, calculated using standard deduction and any additional exemptions.  
4. Eligibility:  
   – Regular employees with a continuous service period of at least 6 months are eligible for the full salary package.  
   – Probationary staff (first 3 months) receive 70% of the basic salary, with all statutory deductions applied.  
5. Exceptions:  
   – Contract staff and interns are paid on a weekly basis, with a minimum pay of ₹15,000 per month.  
   – Remote workers receive salary on the 15th of the month, with a 2% surcharge to cover connectivity costs, subject to managerial approval.  
6. Any salary adjustment, bonus, or incentive will be communicated in a separate memorandum and reflected in the subsequent month’s payslip.

All salaries are paid in Indian Rupees on the last working day of each calendar month (or the next business day if the last day falls on a weekend or public holiday). A payslip is issued electronically within five (5) business days of the salary disbursement and is accessible through the employee portal. The payslip will detail the basic salary, allowances, statutory deductions (10% Professional Tax, 12% EPF, 3% Health & Education Cess), and any other deductions (e.g., advance, loan repayment).

Eligibility: Only full‑time employees with a signed contract are entitled to a regular salary. Probationary staff receive 80% of the agreed basic salary for the first 3 months, after which the full amount is credited. Employees must have completed at least one (1) year of service to qualify for an annual increment of 5%–10% based on performance. No salary may exceed INR 10,00,000 per annum; amounts above this are capped at the maximum limit.  

Exceptions: Interns, volunteers, and short‑term consultants are not eligible for salary; they may receive stipends or reimbursements only for approved expenses. Employees on medical leave are paid a minimum of 90% of their basic salary for up to 30 days, after which the salary is suspended until return to work.

All regular employees are entitled to a gross monthly salary as per their employment contract. The salary is disbursed on or before the 15th of each month via a direct credit to the employee’s nominated bank account. A statutory 5% deduction for provident fund (PF) applies to employees earning up to ₹15,000 per month; above this threshold PF is capped at ₹750. Employees earning more than ₹50,000 per month are subject to an additional 2% Professional Tax deduction up to a maximum of ₹200 per month. Salary components such as Basic, Dearness Allowance (DA), House Rent Allowance (HRA), and Transport Allowance are detailed in the payslip. Payslips are generated electronically and accessible through the intranet portal every 5th of the month. Eligibility for a salary advance of up to 20% of the current month’s basic salary is granted only to full‑time employees who have completed at least six months of continuous service. Exceptions: contractual workers, interns, and outsourced staff receive remuneration on a project‑basis and do not receive a traditional payslip. All deductions are compliant with the Income Tax Act, 1961, and the latest central government

All full‑time employees whose employment contract is active on the last working day of the month are eligible for salary payment on the 30th of that month. Salary is deposited directly into the employee’s bank account. The payslip, containing a detailed breakdown of gross salary, deductions (PF 12%, professional tax ₹200, income tax as per slab), and net amount, is issued electronically on the 5th of the following month. Late payment beyond the 30th incurs a 5 % penalty on the outstanding amount, capped at ₹5,000 per month. Employees on part‑time or contract basis are paid on the 28th of each month, and their payslip is issued on the 3rd of the following month. Exceptions: Employees on maternity leave receive their salary as per the Maternity Benefit Act on the 15th of each month; seasonal workers are paid in bi‑weekly installments with payslips issued within 48 hours of payment. Any discrepancy must be reported within 7 days of receipt.

Salary shall be paid monthly on the 25th of each calendar month. The basic salary is subject to a maximum deduction of 10% for provident fund, 5% for professional tax, and 2% for employee state insurance. Overtime is compensated at 1.5 times the basic hourly rate for hours exceeding 8 per day, capped at 20 hours per week. All employees receive a detailed payslip electronically via the HR portal within 48 hours of the salary disbursement. The payslip includes gross salary, deductions, net pay, leave encashment, and tax deductions. Eligibility for salary increments and bonuses is limited to employees who have completed at least 12 months of continuous service. Employees on contractual or part‑time basis are excluded from the increment scheme unless they convert to a permanent role. In case of salary adjustment due to promotion or role change, the new salary will be effective from the first day of the following month. Salary disputes must be raised within 7 days of receipt of the payslip. The company reserves the right to adjust salary components in compliance with applicable laws.

Salary is credited to the employee’s bank account on or before the 5th working day of each month, based on the salary structure effective from the 1st day of the month. Payslips are emailed within 48 hours of payment and must include Employee ID, basic pay, HRA, dearness allowance, overtime, deductions (PF 12%, ESI 1.75% for salaries above ₹21,000, professional tax, and any loan repayments), and net pay. Overtime is compensated at 1.5× the hourly rate for hours exceeding 8 in a day or 48 in a week, with a cap of ₹10,000 per month. Salary increments are reviewed annually on 31st December, with a minimum increase of 5% for eligible employees. Eligibility for a full salary package requires a minimum of 6 months continuous service and a performance rating of ‘Meets Expectations’ or higher. Employees on probation, interns, and contract workers are exempt from the full salary components; interns receive a stipend capped at ₹5,000/month, and contract workers are paid on the 15th of each month with a maximum deduction limit of 30% of their gross salary for advances or loans. Exceptions to the standard deduction cap are granted only with written managerial approval.

All full‑time employees who have completed a minimum of 3 months of continuous service are eligible for the performance appraisal cycle, conducted twice a year—once at the end of every 6‑month period. Appraisals are scheduled on the last working day of the month following the 6‑month mark and must be completed within 30 calendar days. Each employee’s appraisal is based on a 5‑point scale (1 = Unsatisfactory, 5 = Excellent), with specific KPIs tied to their role (e.g., average handle time, customer satisfaction score, quality audit score). Employees receiving a rating of 4 or 5 are eligible for a salary adjustment of 5 % of their current basic pay; however, the total increase cannot exceed 10 % of the employee’s basic pay in any single appraisal cycle. Bonus payouts, if applicable, are capped at 15 % of the employee’s quarterly commission. Contract staff, interns, and part‑time employees are excluded from the appraisal cycle, except where a managerial position is held on a contractual basis, in which case they are included after 6 months of tenure. All appraisals are documented in the employee’s performance file and reviewed by the HR Manager and the employee’s direct manager.

All employees who have completed a minimum of 6 months of continuous service are eligible for the annual performance appraisal. The appraisal cycle begins on 1 January and ends on 31 December, with a mid‑year review conducted from 1 July to 31 July. Appraisal forms must be submitted within 15 calendar days of the review period’s end. Managers must score each employee on a 1‑5 scale; a composite score of 75 % or higher qualifies the employee for the performance bonus pool, capped at 12 % of the individual’s base salary. Employees scoring below 50 % will be placed on a performance improvement plan (PIP) for 60 days, with a second review on day 60. Employees on probation, interns, and contract staff with a contract length of less than 6 months are exempt from the formal appraisal but will receive a qualitative feedback summary. Exceptions apply for employees on long‑term medical leave or secondment; in such cases, appraisal is deferred until the employee returns or the secondment ends, but the employee remains eligible for bonus consideration if the final score is ≥ 75 %.

Performance appraisal is conducted annually for all employees with a tenure of at least three (3) months, excluding interns, contractors and probationary staff (probation period up to 90 days). The appraisal cycle starts on 1st July and must be completed within forty‑five (45) calendar days after the end of the fiscal year. Each appraisal consists of a 5‑point rating scale (1 = Unsatisfactory to 5 = Excellent), weighted as follows: 80 % manager rating, 10 % employee self‑assessment, 10 % peer review. The final score determines the salary adjustment: 70 % of the score is mapped to the base salary increment and 30 % to the annual bonus pool. The maximum base salary increment is capped at fifteen (15 %) of the current base, but employees in critical roles (IT, Risk, Compliance) may receive up to twenty (20 %) with board approval. A delayed appraisal beyond sixty (60) days disqualifies the employee from any salary hike that year. The annual bonus is limited to ten (10 %) of the base salary, and a performance shortfall can trigger a two (2) percent penalty on the bonus. All appraisal forms and decisions must be recorded in the HRIS within seven (7) days of final approval.

Performance appraisal shall be conducted biannually for all full‑time employees who have completed at least 90 days of service. The appraisal period is the preceding 12 months. Managers must submit appraisal forms within 30 calendar days of the end of the evaluation period. Ratings are on a 5‑point scale; achieving 80% or more of agreed KPI targets results in a rating of 4 or 5. Employees scoring below 3 will trigger a development plan. Bonus eligibility is tied to appraisal: 5% of the employee’s basic salary is earmarked for performance bonus, capped at ₹50,000 per year. Only employees on a regular full‑time contract are eligible; interns, contractors, and part‑time staff are excluded unless they transition to full‑time status before the next appraisal cycle. New hires in their first 6 months after probation are not evaluated for bonus but will receive a probation review after 3 months. The policy is subject to annual review by the HR team.

All employees who have completed at least 90 days of continuous service are eligible for the annual performance appraisal. The appraisal cycle commences on the first Monday of January and concludes by the last business day of February. Each manager will conduct a formal review meeting no later than 10 working days after the employee’s performance review date. Employees must submit a self‑assessment form within 5 calendar days of receiving the appraisal notification. The final performance score is a weighted combination of 70 % manager evaluation, 20 % peer feedback, and 10 % customer satisfaction metrics. Scores are categorized as Outstanding (≥90), Excellent (80–89), Satisfactory (70–79), Needs Improvement (60–69), and Unsatisfactory (<60). Promotions and salary increments are awarded only to those achieving at least Excellent, with a maximum increase of 12 % of base salary. Employees on a performance improvement plan (PIP) for more than 90 days, or those who have received a formal warning, are exempt from promotion consideration until the next appraisal cycle. Part‑time and temporary staff are excluded from the appraisal cycle unless they have been with the company for ≥180 days.

All employees who have successfully completed their probationary period and have been employed for a minimum of six (6) months are eligible for the annual performance appraisal cycle. Appraisals are conducted every twelve (12) months, with the appraisal period running from 1 January to 31 December. Managers must submit performance evaluation forms to HR within thirty (30) calendar days of the end of the appraisal period. The evaluation rubric includes four (4) key performance indicators: quality, productivity, safety compliance, and teamwork, each weighted at 25 %. Employees achieving an overall score of 90 % or above receive a discretionary bonus not exceeding fifteen (15) % of their basic salary. Those scoring between 75 % and 89 % are eligible for a salary increment capped at five (5) % of their current base. Scores below 75 % do not qualify for monetary reward but may receive a developmental plan. Exceptions: (i) Contract workers and temporary hires are excluded from monetary rewards; (ii) Employees on a leave of absence exceeding thirty (30) days during the appraisal period are deferred to the next cycle; (iii) Interns are evaluated for skill acquisition only, without bonus consideration.

Performance appraisal for all full‑time employees of XYZ PSU is conducted annually on the employee’s date of joining anniversary. The appraisal cycle must be completed within 30 calendar days of the anniversary. The appraisal score comprises 70 % of the employee’s bonus eligibility and 30 % of the salary increment recommendation. The maximum permissible salary increment is capped at 15 % of the basic pay for any single appraisal cycle. Employees on probation or in an internship arrangement are excluded from the appraisal process. Employees who have served less than six months at the PSU are deemed ineligible for appraisal until their six‑month mark. Those on medical leave for more than 90 consecutive days will have their appraisal deferred until they return to work. Employees transferred to a different PSU location within the same group are eligible for appraisal only after a 90‑day acclimatization period. All appraisal outcomes are reviewed by the HR Review Committee before final approval.

All full‑time employees who have completed a minimum of 6 months of continuous service with the Company are eligible for the annual performance appraisal cycle. The appraisal will be conducted within 30 days of the end of the fiscal year (31 March) and must be finalized by 31 May. The appraisal process consists of a 90‑day review period during which managers and peers provide feedback, followed by a formal appraisal meeting. Performance ratings are on a 5‑point scale: 1 (Unsatisfactory) to 5 (Outstanding).  

For salary increments, only employees receiving a rating of 4 or 5 are considered for a merit increase. Increment amounts are capped at 12% of the current basic salary. Employees who achieve a rating of 5 may be eligible for an additional discretionary bonus of up to 5% of the annual base salary.  

Employees on a fixed‑term contract, interns, or part‑time staff are excluded from the appraisal. New hires joining after the appraisal deadline will receive a first appraisal in the subsequent fiscal year. Employees who complete their probation within the appraisal window are treated as eligible for the first cycle, but their rating will be based on the probation review.

All employees, contractors, and interns are required to adhere to the company’s Code of Conduct, which includes confidentiality, anti‑harassment, and ethical business practices. Any breach may result in progressive disciplinary action: first offence—written warning; second offence—suspension for 5 days with no pay; third offence—termination of employment. For contractors and interns, the second offence leads directly to contract termination. Salary deductions are capped at 5 % of the monthly basic salary per offence, not exceeding ₹50,000 in total across the employee’s tenure. Confidential data leaks trigger an immediate 7‑day investigation period; if evidence is found, the employee is suspended pending outcome. Eligibility: All permanent and contractual staff are covered; part‑time staff are excluded unless they are handling client data. Exceptions: Emergency situations allowing temporary policy relaxation (e.g., natural disasters) are governed by the Emergency Management Committee and must be documented. Whistleblowers are protected from retaliation and may report anonymously; any retaliation will result in a 30‑day suspension of the offender.

All employees, contractors, and vendors of the Company are required to adhere to the Code of Conduct as a condition of their engagement. Any employee who has been with the Company for less than 12 months is exempt from the “confidentiality breach” penalty clause but must complete the mandatory ethics training within 30 days of hire. For breaches of the Code, the Company will impose a penalty of up to 5% of the employee’s monthly salary, capped at ₹50,000 per incident. Repeated violations (more than two within 12 months) will trigger a suspension of up to 30 days, with the possibility of termination if the conduct remains unrectified. Retail managers and higher-level executives are exempt from the 5% salary penalty but are subject to a 10% bonus reduction for the following fiscal year if the breach involves customer data. All penalties will be applied after a documented investigation and a 7‑day response period for the employee to present mitigating evidence. The Code also permits a one‑time, 24‑hour grace period for employees in remote locations during public holidays to submit required compliance reports.

All employees, contractors and interns of XYZ Pharma Ltd. are expected to adhere to the company’s Code of Conduct at all times. Any breach may result in disciplinary action up to termination. Employees must report conflicts of interest within 5 business days of identification. The company limits personal use of corporate devices for non‑business activities to no more than 2 hours per weekday. In case of non‑compliance with safety protocols, a penalty of 5% of the employee’s monthly salary will be applied, capped at ₹10,000. Whistleblowers are protected under the Whistleblower Protection Act and will not face retaliation. Eligibility: the Code applies to all full‑time and part‑time staff, temporary hires and contractors who have signed the NDA. Exceptions: Senior Management (C‑suite) may have a one‑time, 1‑day exemption for emergency travel that does not affect business operations, subject to prior approval by HR. Employees on maternity leave for up to 12 weeks are exempt from mandatory participation in mandatory safety drills but must attend a briefing within 48 hours of return. The Code is reviewed annually and updated as necessary.

All personnel, including full‑time staff, part‑time employees, interns, and contractors, are expected to uphold the hospital’s Code of Conduct at all times. Any act that undermines patient safety, violates confidentiality, or breaches ethical standards will result in disciplinary action, ranging from a written warning (if the infraction is first‑time and non‑violent) to immediate suspension (for repeat or serious violations). The policy mandates that all staff report incidents within 48 hours; failure to comply may lead to a deduction of up to 10 % of the monthly salary. Attendance is monitored quarterly; employees with more than 5 % absenteeism without valid medical documentation may be considered for termination after a second notice. Confidential information must not be disclosed to external parties; any breach will incur a penalty of Rs. 50,000 or up to 90 days of restricted duties. All employees, officers, and permanent contractors of the PSU are subject to this Code of Conduct. The Code mandates zero tolerance for bribery or kickbacks; any offer of money or gifts exceeding INR 10,000 (or 5 % of the employee’s monthly salary, whichever is lower) must be reported to the Compliance Officer immediately. Employees must maintain confidentiality of all sensitive information; disclosure beyond authorized channels is prohibited, with a maximum penalty of 30 days suspension for first offense and permanent dismissal for repeated violations. Attendance in mandatory training sessions is compulsory; failure to attend two consecutive sessions will result in a written warning and a 5‑day unpaid leave. All gifts or hospitality received must be documented; any value exceeding INR 5,000 is subject to a 15 % tax deduction at source. The Code applies to 100 % of the workforce, except interns and contractual workers with less than 90 days tenure, who are governed by the PSU’s General Employment Policy. Exceptions are granted only with prior written approval from the Ethics Committee for bona‑fide business events.

All employees, including full‑time, part‑time, contract and temporary staff, are expected to adhere to the following Code of Conduct. Any breach may result in progressive disciplinary action, up to termination, within 30 days of written notice. Employees with less than 6 months tenure are not eligible for the “Mentor‑Mentee” privilege, but may access the Ethics Helpline. All employees must complete the annual ethics training (1 hour) within the first 90 days of employment; failure to do so incurs a 5 % deduction of the monthly salary. Overtime is capped at 10 % of the employee’s weekly hours; any overtime beyond 20 % requires managerial approval and will be reimbursed at 1.5× the hourly rate. The maximum fine for policy violations is capped at 15 % of the employee’s annual salary, except in cases of gross negligence where a higher penalty may apply. Exceptions are granted only for lawful compliance, emergencies, or when required by higher authorities; such exceptions must be documented in writing. All conduct policies are reviewed annually and updated in consultation with the Legal and HR departments.

All employees, including contractors and interns, are expected to uphold the highest standards of professional conduct. Employees may not use company equipment for personal calls exceeding 2 hours per week. Repeated violations (more than 3 times in 3 months) will trigger a written warning followed by a 5 % salary deduction for the month of the fourth offense. Attendance must meet a minimum of 95 % of scheduled hours; failure to meet this threshold for 3 consecutive months will result in a formal performance review and possible termination. Employees are prohibited from disclosing confidential client data; a breach will lead to immediate disciplinary action and potential legal liability. Dress code is business casual Monday‑Thursday; on Friday, employees may wear smart casual with a maximum of 1 day per month for non‑managerial staff. Managers may opt for business casual on Fridays subject to manager approval. Social media posts that could reflect negatively on the company are disallowed; any such post must be removed within 24 hours or face disciplinary action. Employees must report any misconduct within 7 days; reports received after 30 days will be deemed invalid. Exceptions apply only to employees in the Customer Experience team, who receive a 10 % extension on personal call limits, and to new hires in their first 60 days, who are exempt from the 5 % penalty for up to 2 infractions.

All employees, including permanent, contractual, and temporary staff, must adhere to the company's Code of Conduct. Attendance must be at least 80% of scheduled working days; any absenteeism exceeding 5 days in a month requires written justification. New hires under the 90‑day probationary period must complete the Ethics and Safety training; failure to do so will result in termination. Any form of bribery, kick‑back, or illicit benefit is strictly prohibited and may lead to immediate dismissal and legal action. Use of company assets for personal gain is forbidden; employees may request permission for personal use of company equipment, limited to 2 hours per week, subject to manager approval. Social media conduct: employees must not post confidential or negative content about the company; violations may lead to disciplinary action. Overtime is capped at 20 hours per month; approval is required from the supervisor and must be compensated at 1.5× regular rate. Exceptions: senior managers (≥5 years tenure) may exceed 20 hours if project‑critical, but must submit justification. Contractors and interns are exempt from the overtime cap but must still follow safety and confidentiality clauses.

All employees, volunteers, board members and contractors of the NGO are required to adhere to the following code of conduct. 1. Attendance: No more than 2 unexcused absences per month and 5 per year. 2. Conflict of interest: Any monetary interest in a contract exceeding ₹50,000 must be declared to the Ethics Committee within 48 hours. 3. Gifts and hospitality: Gifts valued over ₹5,000 must be reported and may not be accepted during a project review period. 4. Social media: No posting of sensitive information; a maximum of 1 post per week about NGO activities is allowed, and all posts must be pre‑approved by the Communications Officer. 5. Dress code: Formal attire is required on board meetings and donor events; otherwise, business casual is permitted. 6. Harassment: Zero‑tolerance policy; any incident must be reported within 24 hours, and the reporting individual is protected against retaliation. 7. Working hours: 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., with a 1‑hour lunch break; overtime requires prior approval and is capped at 10 hours per month. 8. Eligibility: The code applies to all full‑time staff, part‑time staff, volunteers, interns, and board members. 9. Enforcement: Violations may result in written warning, suspension, or termination, depending on severity and prior infractions. All members must sign an acknowledgment of this code annually.

All employees, interns, part‑time staff, contractors, and external auditors of the bank are required to comply with the Code of Conduct.  
**Eligibility** – The Code applies to anyone who has a formal or informal relationship with the bank, except for visitors and guests.  
**Mandatory training** – Each new hire must complete the online Ethics & Compliance module within 30 days of induction. Failure to complete by the deadline results in a 5 % deduction from the following month’s salary, capped at ₹10,000.  
**Gift and hospitality limits** – No employee may accept a gift, entertainment, or hospitality exceeding ₹50,000 in a calendar year. Gifts above this threshold must be reported and may result in suspension up to 30 days.  
**Reporting** – All violations must be reported within 7 calendar days of occurrence. Unreported infractions may lead to a penalty of up to 20 % of the employee’s monthly salary, or termination if the breach is material.  
**Exceptions** – Employees on approved maternity or medical leave are exempt from reporting violations for up to 15 days after return to work. Contractors on a short‑term assignment (<6 months) are exempt from the gift limit if they have no authority to make purchasing decisions.  

The Code is reviewed annually; any amendments require Board approval.

All employees, including permanent, contractual, interns, and part‑time staff, are covered under the POSH policy. The bank shall provide a grievance cell accessible within 7 business days of an incident. The POSH Committee comprises 5 members, with a maximum of 30 % of the total staff, and will not include the accused or immediate supervisor. Each employee must attend a 2‑hour POSH awareness session annually; at least 90 % of employees must complete the session within the first 30 days of employment. Investigations will be concluded within 14 days of receiving a complaint. Penalties include termination for repeated offenses; first offense leads to a 5 % salary deduction for a period not exceeding 3 months. No penalty shall apply to senior executives above 30 years with continuous service over 15 years, provided they have no prior record. The bank reserves the right to exclude any third‑party vendor staff from the policy if the vendor confirms compliance with equivalent standards.

The First Level Committee (FLC) will conduct an inquiry within 15 days from receipt of the complaint and render a decision within 10 days thereafter. The policy applies to any unwanted physical or verbal conduct, including online interactions, that creates a hostile or uncomfortable working environment.  

Employees in managerial or supervisory roles above the 70th percentile of seniority are exempt from the mandatory 30‑minute POSH training, but they must still attend an annual refresher session. All other personnel must complete the 2‑hour POSH training within 30 days of hire and every 12 months thereafter; this training is mandatory for 5 % of the total workforce each year as a compliance measure.  

Penalties for a confirmed case of sexual harassment include a fine of up to 10 % of the offender’s monthly salary, suspension up to 30 days, and possible termination. Victims are entitled to 5 days of paid leave per incident and are protected against retaliation. The policy is reviewed annually by the HR and Legal departments to ensure alignment with the Sexual Harassment at Workplace (POSH) Act and relevant labor regulations.

Sexual harassment is strictly prohibited. All employees, trainees, interns, contractors, and vendors working on company premises or under company contracts are covered. Non‑employees such as suppliers or visitors are not covered unless they are present on company premises for work purposes.  

If an employee experiences or witnesses harassment, they must report to the POSH Committee within **15 calendar days** of the incident. The Committee shall investigate and provide a written report within **30 days**. Sanctions for the harasser may include a fine up to **5% of the monthly salary**, suspension for up to **30 days**, or termination if the conduct is severe or repeats.  

Employees who report harassment will be protected from retaliation. The company will not dismiss, demote, or alter employment terms of the complainant.  

The policy applies to all departments; however, part‑time employees earning less than **₹50,000 per month** are exempt from fine provisions but still subject to disciplinary action. The policy is reviewed annually and amended as per the POSH Act, 2013.

All employees, contractors, interns and vendors who have worked at the chain for a minimum of 6 months are eligible to be part of the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC). The ICC shall comprise at least 30 % women and 70 % men, with a maximum of 10 % of total staff. At least one senior executive (not exceeding 2 % of workforce) and two junior staff members must be included. The ICC must be constituted within 15 days of policy issuance. Any allegation of sexual harassment must be filed in writing within 30 calendar days of the incident. The investigation will be completed within 60 days, and a written report will be delivered to the complainant. If the complainant is a senior manager, the policy applies but the investigation may be escalated to the Board. Penalties for confirmed violations include a mandatory suspension of 2 weeks and possible termination, plus civil and criminal liability. All employees, interns, trainees and contractual staff engaged with the PSU for a minimum of 3 months are covered under the POSH policy. Complaints of sexual harassment must be filed within 30 days from the incident. An internal investigation will be initiated within 7 days of the complaint and concluded within 60 days. If harassment is proven, the offending party may face a penalty of 5 % of their monthly salary, capped at Rs. 10,000. The policy allows a maximum of three separate complaints per employee per calendar year to be processed. The POSH committee will include at least 30 % of senior and middle‑management members to ensure representation. All investigations are confidential and any retaliatory action against the complainant will be treated as a separate disciplinary case. 

Eligibility rules: the policy applies to all staff, including part‑time and remote workers, provided they spend at least 20 % of their work time at the PSU premises. Exceptions: (i) employees who have been with the PSU for less than 3 months, (ii) senior executives above 55 years of age, and (iii) contractors who are not present on the PSU premises for more than 80 % of their contractual period, are exempt from mandatory POSH training but are required to report any incidents promptly.

The hospital shall establish a POSH Committee comprising 5 members: a senior manager, an HR representative, a senior medical officer, an external gender‑equity expert, and a legal counsel. All employees, contractors, interns, temporary staff and visitors (excluding independent contractors and individuals under 18 years of age) are covered by the POSH policy.  
The company shall form a Grievance Committee (GC) of at least five members: 1 HR representative, 1 senior manager, 1 employee of the complainant’s department (non‑supervisor), 1 external expert (law or NGOs) and 1 senior legal counsel. At least 30 % of GC members must be women, and no GC member may directly supervise the complainant or the alleged respondent.  

A complaint must be filed in writing within **5 calendar days** of the incident. The GC will investigate and deliver a written report within **15 days** of receipt. If the GC cannot resolve the issue internally, the matter will be referred to an external committee under the Act, and a final decision will be rendered within **30 days**.  

The policy provides a 10 % cap on the number of employees who may serve on the GC at any time. Any employee who withdraws a complaint within **7 days** of filing will not face disciplinary action. The policy applies to all forms of sexual harassment—including verbal, physical, non‑physical, and online conduct—and is enforceable under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, etc.) Act, 2013.

Any staff member, volunteer, or intern may lodge a grievance in writing to HR within 30 calendar days of the alleged incident. HR must acknowledge receipt within 3 working days and initiate an investigation. The investigation should be completed and a resolution communicated within 15 working days, unless the matter requires further inquiry, in which case the resolution period may be extended up to 30 days with prior approval. The policy applies to all employees, volunteers, interns, and contractors, except for senior management whose grievances are directed to the Board. The maximum financial liability for compensation under this policy is capped at INR 1,00,000 per incident, and no compensation will exceed 20 % of the employee’s monthly salary. Grievances related to political affiliations, religious beliefs, or personal disputes unrelated to work are excluded. All resolved grievances are documented, and 70 % of cases are expected to reach closure within the 15‑day window. The policy is governed by Indian labour laws and the NGO’s statutory guidelines.

Grievances may be submitted by any full‑time employee (excluding interns and contractors) within 30 calendar days from the incident.  The employee must lodge a written complaint with the HR HelpDesk, which will acknowledge receipt within 48 hours and assign a unique reference number.  The first level of review (HR Manager) must be completed within 10 business days, with a written decision returned to the complainant.  If the grievance remains unresolved, it is escalated to the Senior HR Director within 15 business days of the initial review, and a final decision is rendered within 7 days of escalation.  

All complaints are treated confidentially; the complainant and respondent are notified of the outcome but names are disclosed only if the complainant consents or if required by law.  Compensation claims under this policy are capped at 20% of the employee’s monthly salary, with a maximum of ₹2,00,000 per incident.  

Exceptions: Grievances involving personal disputes outside the workplace, or those arising from disciplinary actions, are excluded from the formal grievance procedure and are handled per the Code of Conduct.  Contractors may file grievances only through the designated Contractor Liaison Officer and are subject to a 60‑day filing window.

All employees of the bank are eligible to file a grievance through the established Grievance Redressal System. Grievances can be submitted in writing (email or physical form) within 30 days of the incident. The first level of resolution is an informal meeting with the immediate supervisor, to be completed within 5 business days. If unresolved, the grievance is escalated to the Departmental Grievance Committee, which must review and decide within 15 calendar days of receipt. The Committee will issue a written decision; if the employee is dissatisfied, a second level appeal to the HR Grievance Board is available within 7 days of the Committee’s decision. The final decision of the Board is binding and must be communicated within 20 calendar days of the appeal submission.

Financial redress is capped at a maximum of Rs. 50,000 per case, subject to a 5% surcharge on the amount claimed. All decisions are documented and retained for a minimum of 3 years. Exceptions apply for grievances involving senior management (above Grade 9), where a separate Executive Grievance Panel will convene, and for matters of legal or regulatory nature, which will be referred to the bank’s Legal Department immediately. All grievances are handled confidentially, and retaliation against a complainant is strictly prohibited.

All full‑time employees and interns are eligible to lodge a grievance. Contractual and temporary staff may file only under the “special grievance” clause. The grievance must be submitted in writing to the employee’s immediate manager within 14 days of the incident. The manager must acknowledge receipt within 7 days and resolve the issue or forward it to HR within an additional 7 days. HR will review, provide a written response within 14 days, and, if unresolved, refer to the Grievance Committee (GC) within 30 days of the original filing. The GC, comprising one senior manager, one HR lead, and an external mediator, must deliver a final decision within 45 days. For claims involving monetary compensation exceeding ₹5 lakhs, the GC will seek court‑advised settlement within 60 days.

All grievances are treated with 100 % confidentiality. The company will not disclose the identity of the complainant or respondent until the grievance is formally closed, unless required by law. Exceptions: Sexual harassment, whistle‑blower complaints, and discrimination cases are escalated immediately to the GC without the manager’s review and may trigger an external investigator. Failure to comply with the timeline by the manager or HR may result in a 5 % penalty of the employee’s monthly basic salary, unless excused by documented medical or operational reasons.

All employees, excluding interns, contractual or temporary staff, are entitled to file a grievance through the designated channel within 30 days of the incident. The grievance must be submitted in writing to the immediate supervisor, who shall forward it to the HR grievance portal within 48 hours. The HR grievance committee (comprising the HR manager, a senior staff representative, and an external legal advisor) will acknowledge receipt within 5 business days and commence investigation. The committee aims to resolve 70% of grievances within 30 days and 90% within 60 days. If the resolution exceeds the 60‑day window, a written report will be issued detailing reasons for delay. Compensation limits are capped at 5% of the employee’s annual basic salary or INR 5,00,000, whichever is lower, for financial redress. No retaliation is permitted; violations will lead to disciplinary action. Senior officers and directors are exempt from the 48‑hour forwarding requirement but must submit grievances directly to the committee. Appeals may be lodged within 15 days of the final decision, subject to a separate review panel.

All permanent and contractual employees (except interns and third‑party contractors) are entitled to lodge a grievance. A grievance may be submitted in writing or via the company intranet portal and must include the employee’s name, designation, date, description of issue and supporting documents. The Grievance Committee (GC) shall review and respond to the first level grievance within 30 calendar days of receipt. If the employee is unsatisfied, the GC may refer the matter to the Senior Grievance Committee (SGC), which must issue a decision within 60 calendar days. For matters requiring immediate remediation (e.g., safety violations), the GC will expedite resolution within 15 days. The company commits to a 90 % resolution rate on all grievances within 60 days. Compensation for damages shall not exceed 5 % of the employee’s monthly basic salary, except for cases involving gross misconduct where the limit is 10 %. Employees in managerial or senior management positions are excluded from the GC process and must raise concerns directly with the Director of Human Resources. The policy remains in force until superseded by a revised version.

All grievances must be filed in writing (email or online portal) within 30 calendar days of the incident. The employee’s immediate supervisor shall acknowledge receipt within 48 hours and initiate a preliminary review. If the grievance remains unresolved after 7 calendar days, it will be escalated to the Department Head; a response is required within 14 days. For matters not satisfactorily resolved at the departmental level, the company’s Grievance Committee (comprising HR, Legal, and an employee representative) will conduct a full investigation within 30 calendar days from the date of escalation.  

Eligible employees include full‑time, part‑time, and contract staff who have completed at least 90 days of continuous service. Interns, temporary workers, and outsourced personnel are excluded unless they are directly employed by the company. Exemptions apply to senior executives (above the 8th level), who must seek resolution through the Board’s Mediation Panel.  

If the grievance involves monetary compensation, the company will award up to 5% of the employee’s annual basic salary, capped at ₹50,000. For non‑monetary relief, the committee may order corrective action, retraining, or a written apology. All decisions are final after the 30‑day review and may be appealed to the Arbitration Board within 15 days of notification.

Employees who believe their rights have been infringed or who have experienced workplace grievances must submit a written complaint to the HR grievance officer within **15 calendar days** from the date of the incident. Complaints received after 15 days may still be considered if they are related to **sexual harassment, discrimination, or whistle‑blowing**, provided a supporting document is attached.  

All complaints will be acknowledged within **48 hours** of receipt and investigated within **10 business days**. The HR officer shall provide a written resolution or action plan within **30 days** of the initial complaint. The company aims to resolve **95 % of grievances within 30 days** and **100 % within 60 days**.  

Eligibility: Employees must have been with the company for at least **3 months** and be in good standing (no disciplinary action in the last 6 months).  
Limit: Compensation or disciplinary actions resulting from a grievance shall not exceed **10 % of the employee’s monthly salary**.  

Exceptions:  
1. Complaints of **sexual harassment, caste, gender or religious discrimination, or whistle‑blowing** are exempt from the 15‑day filing window.  
2. Grievances involving **confidential or security matters** may be addressed within **5 business days** and will be handled by a senior manager.  

All decisions are final after the **HR grievance committee** (including a senior manager and a union representative) has issued a written recommendation.

Any employee who believes that a policy has been breached, or that they have suffered any form of discrimination, harassment, unfair treatment, or workplace injury, may lodge a formal grievance. A written complaint must be submitted to the immediate supervisor and copied to the HR Manager within **7 days** of the incident. The HR Manager will acknowledge receipt within **24 hours** and initiate an investigation. The investigation shall be concluded and a written decision delivered to the complainant within **30 calendar days** from the date of acknowledgement. If the grievance is found to be valid and requires remedial action, the action must be taken within **14 days** of the decision, except in cases involving serious misconduct (e.g., sexual harassment, theft, or violence), where the matter is referred to the Police and the investigation may extend beyond 30 days.

Only employees with a minimum tenure of **90 days** are eligible to file a grievance; contractors and part‑time staff are covered under separate clauses. The maximum monetary compensation that can be awarded under a grievance claim is capped at **₹50,000**. Any claim exceeding this limit will be treated as a separate legal matter. 

If a grievance remains unresolved after 30 days, the employee’s supervisor will receive a performance penalty of **5%** of their monthly salary for non‑resolution, unless the delay is justified by external legal or regulatory proceedings.
